definition_zh: 烤箱；烤炉；灶；窑炉
definition_en: an enclosed chamber that is heated so that food can be baked inside it, and by extension any similar heated chamber used in industry or felt as unbearable heat
core_image: 玻璃门内一团橙光，铁架上的面团正慢慢鼓起
scene: 冬夜的厨房里，玻璃门内透出橙黄的光，铁架上的面团一点点鼓起来。 He lifted the lid and a wave of heat rolled out of the oven.
sceneCN: 这里 oven 是「烤箱」（第 1 个义项：家里用来烘焙食物的封闭炉箱）；句意为他掀开盖子，一股热气从烤箱里滚出来，画面是玻璃门内那团橙光和鼓起来的面团。

derivatives.zh: 由 oven 与 -proof 复合而成，义为「耐烤箱高温的」
由 oven 与 -ware 复合而成，义为「烤箱用器皿」
由 oven 与 ready 复合而成，义为「可直接入炉烤制的」

senses.title: A heated box for baking food at home
senses.definition: an enclosed part of a cooker, heated by gas or electricity, in which food is baked or roasted
senses.definitionCN: 炉灶上用燃气或电加热的封闭部分，用来烘烤或烤制食物
senses.example: She slid the tray into the hot oven and set the timer.
senses.exampleCN: 她把烤盘推进滚烫的烤箱，定了时。
senses.why: Old English ofen named a heated clay chamber, so the core picture is a closed box holding heat rather than a machine; baking is simply what such a box was built to do.
senses.whyCN: 古英语 ofen 指用火加热的泥土密室，所以这个词的底图是一只拢住热气的封闭箱子，而不是一台机器；烘焙只是这种箱子本来就承担的事，因此「烤箱」是最贴近底图的义项。

senses.title: The baking compartment of a cooker
senses.definition: the part of a kitchen stove that is closed off and heated for baking, as distinct from the burners on top
senses.definitionCN: 厨房炉灶上封闭加热、专门用于烘烤的部分，与上方的明火灶眼相对
senses.example: The casserole sat in the lower oven of the cooker.
senses.exampleCN: 炖锅放在炉灶下面那层烤室里。
senses.why: A cooker repeats the old chamber in miniature and puts it under the burners, so the word moves from a whole hearth to one compartment of a kitchen range.
senses.whyCN: 炉灶把旧式的加热室缩小后安在灶眼下面，于是这个词从整座火塘转到厨房灶具的一个隔间；词义缩小，指的还是那只装热气的箱子。

senses.title: An industrial chamber for firing or drying
senses.definition: a large heated chamber used in industry for firing clay, drying materials or turning coal into coke
senses.definitionCN: 工业上用的大型加热室，用于烧制陶土、烘干物料或把煤炼成焦炭
senses.example: A coke oven burns coal slowly to produce coke for steel making.
senses.exampleCN: 炼焦炉把煤慢慢加热，为炼钢生产焦炭。
senses.why: Brick ovens and coke ovens enlarge the same chamber and trap heat around clay or coal instead of dough, so the name follows the shape of the box rather than the food inside.
senses.whyCN: 砖窑与炼焦炉把同一只加热室放大，把热气拢在陶土或煤的周围而不是面团周围；名字跟着箱子的形状走，不跟着里面的东西走，于是义项从厨房扩到工厂。

senses.title: A room or place that feels unbearably hot
senses.definition: a room or enclosed space that is so hot and airless that it feels like the inside of an oven
senses.definitionCN: 热而不透风的房间或封闭空间，待在里面像待在烤箱里一样
senses.example: The attic was an oven by noon.
senses.exampleCN: 到了中午，阁楼热得像烤箱。
senses.why: The comparison works by sensation rather than by cooking: a person standing in a closed hot room feels the same blast that comes out when an oven door opens, so the word crosses over to discomfort.
senses.whyCN: 这个比喻靠的是体感而不是烹饪：人站在不透风的闷热房间里，感到的正是烤箱门打开时扑出的那股热浪，所以这个词跨到「难受的闷热」这一边。

intro.en: Oven is an inherited Germanic word for a heated chamber, and its recorded history in English reaches back to the first written texts.
intro.cn: oven 是日耳曼语中表示「加热密室」的固有词，它在英语里的记录可以上溯到最早的文献。

items.en: A form usually reconstructed as ufnaz or uhnaz gave the Germanic languages their word for a baking chamber, though the exact shape of the reconstruction is uncertain.
items.cn: 一般把日耳曼语的这个词重构为 ufnaz 或 uhnaz，意为烘焙用的加热室，但重构的确切形式仍有争议。

items.en: Old English ofen named a dome-shaped chamber of clay or stone with a fire lit inside it.
items.cn: 古英语 ofen 指圆顶的泥土或石头加热室，火就生在室内。

items.en: Middle English kept both the sense and the spelling, and a village often shared one large oven for the whole week's bread.
items.cn: 中古英语保留原义与原拼写，一个村子常常共用一座大炉烤一整周的面包。

items.en: Iron ranges brought a smaller oven indoors beside the fire, and the word settled into the kitchen.
items.cn: 铁炉灶把较小的烤室搬进室内、安在火边，这个词就此落进厨房。

items.en: Gas, electric and microwave ovens still name the same closed chamber, while a sweltering room is also called an oven.
items.cn: 燃气炉、电烤箱与微波炉沿用的仍是那只封闭加热室，而闷热的房间也被叫作 oven。

note.en: The look-alike group collects compounds built directly on the noun; the near-meaning group collects other chambers and appliances that produce or hold heat.
note.cn: 形近组收直接由这个名词构成的复合词；近义组收其他产生热量或拢住热量的炉具与炉室。

entries.definitionCN: 用于高温烧制陶器、砖或石灰的窑。

entries.definition: An appliance that heats food with electromagnetic waves instead of a flame.
entries.definitionCN: 用电磁波而非明火加热食物的炉具。

normalIntro.en: The word names a box that holds heat, and its hooks return to the chamber, its fuel and the compounds built on it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词说的是「拢住热气的箱子」，记忆钩子都回到那间加热室、它的燃料，以及由它构成的复合词。

normal.en: Old English ofen and German Ofen are cousins, so the word has meant a heated chamber for more than a thousand years.
normal.cn: 古英语 ofen 与德语 Ofen 是同源词，所以这个词指加热室已有一千多年。

normal.en: The noun names the box, not the fuel, which is why wood, gas and electric versions all keep one name.
normal.cn: 这个名词命名的是箱子而不是燃料，所以柴火、燃气与电热的版本共用一个名字。

normal.en: Ovenproof adds a suffix meaning resistant, so the word describes what the heat cannot do to the dish.
normal.cn: ovenproof 加上表示「抗得住」的后缀，说的是高温拿这只盘子没办法。

normal.en: Microwave oven puts the new heating method in front of the old noun instead of inventing a fresh word.
normal.cn: microwave oven 把新的加热方式摆在旧名词前面，而没有另造新词。

normal.en: A room called an oven borrows only the heat of the box, not its shape or its purpose.
normal.cn: 被叫作 oven 的房间只借了箱子的热度，不借它的形状与用途。

abstract.en: A baker drawing a long wooden peel out of a brick mouth shows the word before it entered the kitchen.

abstract.en: A closed attic at noon shows the word sliding from cooking to plain discomfort.

definition_zh: 兴奋；激动；刺激；令人兴奋的事
definition_en: a feeling of great eagerness or strong emotion, or something that produces this feeling
core_image: 开场铃响前挤满人的游乐场：心跳加速，谁也站不住
scene: 游乐园的过山车缓缓爬到最高点，车厢里所有人屏住呼吸，随后尖叫声混着笑声炸开，谁也安静不下来。 The excitement of the ride kept him buzzing all afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里 excitement 指「强烈的兴奋情绪」（第 1 个义项：又期待又紧张的心理状态）；句意为过山车的刺激让他整个下午都兴奋难平。

derivatives.zh: 使激动；激起（excitement 的动词根，义为「把情绪唤出来」）

senses.title: The state of strong eagerness
senses.definition: a state of feeling excited, eager, and often unable to stay calm
senses.definitionCN: 既期待又紧张、难以保持平静的心理状态
senses.example: The excitement of the ride kept him buzzing all afternoon.
senses.exampleCN: 游乐设施的刺激让他整个下午都兴奋难平。
senses.why: The suffix -ment turns the verb into a thing: the stirred water becomes the swirling you can feel inside.
senses.whyCN: 后缀 -ment 把动词变成名词：被搅动的水面变成体内能感觉到的翻腾。

senses.title: Something that causes strong feeling
senses.definition: an event or thing that produces excitement
senses.definitionCN: 会让人兴奋起来的事件或事物
senses.example: The trip added a new excitement to the quiet summer.
senses.exampleCN: 这次旅行给安静的夏天添了一份新刺激。
senses.why: Once the feeling is a noun, it can also mean its own source: the stir names both the wave and the stone.
senses.whyCN: 情绪成为名词后也可指其来源：这个词既指波浪，也指石头。

senses.title: Public unrest or turmoil
senses.definition: a situation of public agitation or nervous activity
senses.definitionCN: 公众情绪被搅起、人心不稳的局面
senses.example: The rumour caused great excitement in the town.
senses.exampleCN: 谣言在镇上引起了极大的骚动。
senses.why: When many waters ripple at once, the name covers the social storm too.
senses.whyCN: 当许多水面同时起波澜，这个词也覆盖了社会层面的风暴。

intro.en: Excitement is the verb excite plus the noun suffix -ment, formed in English from Latin stock.
intro.cn: excitement 即动词 excite 加名词后缀 -ment，在英语中由拉丁词干构成。

items.en: The root is excitare "to rouse", from ciere "to move, to summon".
items.cn: 词根是 excitare「唤起」，来自 ciere「使动、召唤」。

items.en: French had exciter and excitements, carrying both feeling and agitation.
items.cn: 法语有 exciter 与 excitements，兼指情绪与骚动。

items.en: The noun excitements appears in English in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 名词 excitements 于十五世纪见于英语。

items.en: Modern English uses it mainly for the feeling, with the older unrest sense kept in formal prose.
items.cn: 现代英语主要用于情绪义，骚动义保留在正式文体中。

items.en: The -ment suffix marks the result state: after the stone falls, this is what the water does.
items.cn: 后缀 -ment 标记结果状态：石落之后，水面由此翻腾。

note.en: Nearby nouns name similar stirred-up states of mind.
note.cn: 相邻名词同样指被搅起的心理状态。

examples.en: The crowd buzzed with excitement before the show.
examples.cn: 演出开始前，人群兴奋得嗡嗡作响。

examples.en: The rumour caused great excitement in the town.
examples.cn: 谣言在镇上引起了极大的骚动。

examples.en: The trip added a new excitement to the quiet summer.
examples.cn: 这次旅行给安静的夏天添了一份新刺激。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「一颗赛特门」——赛点之门一开，全场沸腾冲进去。

sensesIntro.en: The word names the stirred feeling, its fun sources, and public unrest.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词既指被搅起的情绪，也指带来刺激的事物与社会骚动。

definition_zh: 创造；创作；创建；造成
definition_en: to make something new that did not exist before
core_image: 从无到有，把新东西造出来
scene: 美术课上，老师让我们用废旧纸盒搭建一座小城堡。 Our class will create a model city from old boxes.
sceneCN: 这里 create 是「创造；创作」（第 1 个义项：做出以前不存在的新东西）；句意是我们班要用旧纸盒创作一座模型城市。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ion 构成，义为「创造；作品」
由 create 加 -ive 构成，义为「有创造力的」
由 create 加 -or 构成，义为「创造者」
同源词，义为「生物；动物」
由 creative 加 -ity 构成，义为「创造力」

senses.title: To make something new from nothing
senses.titleCN: 从无到有地造出新东西
senses.definition: to bring something into existence that was not there before
senses.definitionCN: 使以前不存在的东西出现
senses.example: The writer created a brave little hero for her story.
senses.exampleCN: 作家为故事创造了一个勇敢的小主角。
senses.why: The core image is bringing a thing into the world for the first time, so create means to make what was not.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是第一次把一个东西带到世上，所以 create 意为造出原本没有的。

senses.title: To set up an organisation or system
senses.definition: to start or establish something such as a group, a law or a plan
senses.definitionCN: 建立或设立团体、法规、计划等
senses.example: The school created a new club for young painters.
senses.exampleCN: 学校为年轻绘画爱好者创建了一个新社团。
senses.why: A club does not exist until people act to bring it together, so founding is also creating.
senses.whyCN: 社团在被人们组织起来之前并不存在，所以创立也是创造。

senses.title: To cause trouble or difficulty
senses.definition: to make a problem or difficult situation appear
senses.definitionCN: 使问题或困难出现
senses.example: Leaving the tap on can create a big mess.
senses.exampleCN: 不关水龙头会造成大麻烦。
senses.why: The power of making things also applies to bad results, so the same verb covers problems.
senses.whyCN: 「造出东西」的能力同样适用于坏结果，所以这个动词也覆盖问题。

intro.en: Create comes from a Latin verb that meant to bring forth or make grow.
intro.cn: create 来自拉丁语动词，意为使产生、使生长。

items.en: The Latin creare meant to make or produce, probably linked to crescere, to grow.
items.cn: 拉丁语 creare 意为制造、产出，一般认为与 crescere（生长）相关。

items.en: From it came creatura, anything brought into being, a creature.
items.cn: 由此派生 creatura，指被造之物，即生物。

items.en: English borrowed createn in the fourteenth century, at first often about God making the world.
items.cn: 英语在十四世纪借入 createn，起初常指上帝创造世界。

items.en: The verb widened to artists, builders and founders.
items.cn: 动词义扩展到艺术家、建造者和创立者。

items.en: Today create covers art, jobs, systems and problems alike.
items.cn: 如今 create 覆盖艺术、就业、系统和问题。

note.en: These words share the create root or name making new things.
note.cn: 这些词与 create 同根，或指造出新事物。

abstract.cn: 看空白的纸页在笔尖下长出整个故事。

abstract.en: Watch empty shelves become a paper city in art class.
abstract.cn: 看美术课上的空纸盒变成一座纸城。

abstract.en: Picture a single tap left open, and trouble grows out of one drop.
abstract.cn: 想象没关紧的水龙头，麻烦从一滴水长出来。

examples.cn: 学生们为地球日创作了一张海报。

examples.en: This app helps you create your own music.
examples.cn: 这款应用帮你创作自己的音乐。

examples.en: Crowded rooms can create noise problems.
examples.cn: 拥挤的房间会造成噪音问题。

sensesIntro.cn: 从造新物，到创立系统，再到引起麻烦。

definition_zh: 打印机；印刷工；印刷厂；照片冲印师
definition_en: a machine that prints text or pictures onto paper; a person who sets type and runs a press; a firm that produces printed matter; also a person who makes photographic prints
core_image: 纸从机器里一寸寸滑出来，字迹还带着墨的温热
scene: 深夜的办公室里只剩一盏台灯，最后一叠白纸被塞进机器，指示灯一闪一闪。 The printer hummed for a moment and pushed out the last page of the report.
sceneCN: 这里 printer 指「打印机」（第 1 个义项：把文字和图像印到纸上的机器）；句意为打印机嗡响片刻，吐出了报告的最后一项内容。图中可辨识物件：台灯、白纸、闪着的指示灯。

pos.zh: 打印机；印刷工；印刷厂；照片冲印师

derivatives.zh: 由动词 print 加名词后缀 -ing 构成，义为「印刷；印刷业」，与 printer 同族
由 print 与 out 复合而成，义为「打印出来的文件；打印稿」
由 print 加后缀 -able 构成，义为「可印刷的；适合印出来的」

senses.title: A machine that prints text or images onto paper
senses.definition: a machine, usually connected to a computer, that puts text or pictures onto paper
senses.definitionCN: 通常与计算机相连、把文字或图像印到纸上的机器
senses.example: The printer ran out of paper halfway through the chapter.
senses.exampleCN: 印到这一章一半时，打印机没纸了。
senses.why: The ending -er marks the one that performs an action, and English has long let that ending cover tools as well as people, so the box that does the printing takes over the name of the hand that once did it.
senses.whyCN: 词尾 -er 标记「执行动作的那一个」，而英语早就允许它同时指工具和人，所以这台替人完成印刷的盒子沿用了从前那只手的名字。

senses.title: A person whose trade is setting type and running a press
senses.definition: a worker who arranges type and operates a printing press
senses.definitionCN: 负责排字并操作印刷机的工人
senses.example: Her grandfather was a printer who could read type upside down.
senses.exampleCN: 她祖父是印刷工，能倒着读字模。
senses.why: Before machines, printing was work of the hands: one man set the letters, another pulled the bar, and whoever owned that skill was simply called the printer.
senses.whyCN: 在有机器之前，印刷全靠一双手：有人拣字，有人扳动杠杆，掌握这门手艺的人就被称作印刷工，这是最老的一层意思。

senses.title: A firm that produces printed matter
senses.definition: a business that prints books, newspapers or other material for clients
senses.definitionCN: 替客户印书、印报或印其他材料的商号
senses.example: The book was sent to a printer in the next town.
senses.exampleCN: 这本书被送到邻镇的印刷厂。
senses.why: Once the trade gathered into workshops with several presses, the same word moved from the craftsman to the business he ran, because a customer dealt with the shop and not with one pair of hands.
senses.whyCN: 当这门手艺聚成拥有几台印刷机的作坊，同一个词就从手艺人转到他经营的商号，因为客户打交道的是那家店，而不是某一双手。

senses.title: A person who makes photographic prints
senses.definition: a person who produces final photographic prints from negatives or digital files
senses.definitionCN: 把底片或数字文件做成最终照片的人
senses.example: The printer adjusted the exposure before making the final copy.
senses.exampleCN: 冲印师在出最终成片前调整了曝光。
senses.why: Photography borrowed the word because a photographic print is also an image pressed onto treated paper, so whoever makes the final copy inherited the old title.
senses.whyCN: 摄影借用了这个词，因为照片同样是把影像压到处理过的纸上，于是负责做出最终成片的人继承了旧称呼。

intro.en: Printer is print plus an old agent ending, and print itself is usually traced through French to a Latin verb meaning to press, so the word starts from pressure rather than from ink.
intro.cn: printer 是 print 加一个古老的表人词尾；print 一般认为经法语上溯到表示「压」的拉丁语动词，所以这个词的起点是压力，而不是墨水。

items.en: The Latin verb premere meant to press, squeeze or push down, and its participle pressus stands behind the whole family of press words.
items.cn: 拉丁语动词 premere 意为压、挤、按下，它的分词 pressus 支撑起 press 一族词。

items.en: Adding the prefix in- to premere produced imprimere, to press something into a surface, which is the picture behind every kind of printing.
items.cn: 在 premere 前加前缀 in- 得到 imprimere，意为把某物压进一个表面，这正是各种印刷背后的画面。

items.en: Old French used the noun preinte for an impression or a mark, and the verb preindre for making one; English took the noun first.
items.cn: 古法语用名词 preinte 指印痕、印记，动词 preindre 指压出印记；英语先借的是名词。

items.en: Middle English printen first meant to make a mark by pressure, and only later narrowed to pressing inked type onto paper.
items.cn: 中古英语 printen 最初指用压力留下痕迹，后来才缩小为把沾墨的字模压到纸上。

items.en: The agent ending -er first named the man at the press, and from the nineteenth century the same word was stretched to the machines that do the pressing for him.
items.cn: 表人的词尾 -er 先指站在印刷机旁的人；从十九世纪起，同一个词又被扩展到替他完成压印的机器上。

note.en: The look-alike group follows the print family and the Latin pressing stem; the near-meaning group gathers the other machines and trades that put marks on paper.
note.cn: 形近组沿着 print 词族与拉丁语表示「压」的词干展开；近义组收其他在纸上留下痕迹的机器与行当。

entries.definition: To press inked type or an image onto paper; the verb that printer is built on.
entries.definitionCN: 把沾墨的字模或图像压到纸上；printer 正是由这个动词构成。

entries.definition: The act or trade of producing printed matter.
entries.definitionCN: 生产印刷品的活动或行业。

entries.definition: A page or set of pages produced by a computer printer.
entries.definitionCN: 由计算机打印出来的纸页。

entries.definition: A mark pressed into a surface, or to press such a mark.
entries.definitionCN: 压进表面的印记，或压出这样的印记。

entries.definition: A machine that presses inked type onto paper, especially in a printing house.
entries.definitionCN: 把沾墨字模压到纸上的机器，尤指印刷厂的印刷机。

entries.definition: A machine that makes paper copies of documents.
entries.definitionCN: 把文件复制到纸上的机器。

entries.definition: A machine with keys that strike type onto paper.
entries.definitionCN: 用按键把字模打到纸上的机器。

entries.definition: A device that turns a printed page into a digital image, the opposite direction from a printer.
entries.definitionCN: 把纸页变成数字图像的设备，方向与打印机相反。

normalIntro.en: The word is an old agent ending laid on a verb that came from Latin pressing, so its reminders keep returning to pressure and to the hand that used to supply it.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是古老表人词尾加在一个源自拉丁语「压」的动词上，所以记忆线索总是回到压力和从前提供压力的那只手。

normal.en: Print comes from a Latin verb for pressing, so printing began as pressing rather than as writing.
normal.cn: print 出自拉丁语表示「压」的动词，所以印刷最初是压，而不是写。

normal.en: The -er in printer marks the one that does the action, the same ending as in teacher and builder.
normal.cn: printer 里的 -er 标记执行动作的那一个，和 teacher、builder 用的是同一个词尾。

normal.en: The machine sense is that same ending stretched to a tool, the way a computer is called a server.
normal.cn: 机器义只是把同一个词尾伸到工具身上，就像计算机被叫作 server 一样。

normal.en: Old French preinte gave English the noun print, and the t at the end is the trace of that borrowed participle.
normal.cn: 古法语 preinte 给英语送来了名词 print，词尾的 t 就是那个借来的分词留下的痕迹。

normal.en: Imprint keeps the Latin prefix in-: to press a mark into something.
normal.cn: imprint 保留了拉丁语前缀 in-，意思是把印记压进去。

abstract.en: A printer is a hand that became a box: the same job, the same pressure, only faster.
abstract.cn: 打印机是一只变成盒子的手：同样的活，同样的压力，只是更快。

abstract.en: Every printed page records two surfaces being pushed together, which is why the word belongs to the body before it belongs to the office.
abstract.cn: 每一页印刷品都记录着两个表面互相挤压，所以这个词先属于身体，后来才属于办公室。

abstract.en: When a word for a person turns into a word for a machine, a trade has been rebuilt around its tool.
abstract.cn: 当一个指人的词变成指机器的词，说明一门手艺已经围绕它的工具被重新搭建。

examples.en: The printer ran out of paper halfway through the chapter.
examples.cn: 印到这一章一半时，打印机没纸了。

examples.en: Her grandfather was a printer who could read type upside down.
examples.cn: 她祖父是印刷工，能倒着读字模。

examples.en: The book was sent to a printer in the next town.
examples.cn: 这本书被送到邻镇的印刷厂。

dict_mnemonic.text: 谐音「普林特」——噗的一声，纸从机器里滑出来，那就是 printer。

root: print（印刷）加表人后缀 -er；print 经中古英语 printen、古法语 preinte 上溯到拉丁语 premere（压），加前缀 in- 的 imprimere 意为压印。

sensesIntro.en: The core is pressure transferring a mark; the senses divide into the machine that presses, the worker who once pressed, the firm that owns the presses, and the photographer who presses an image onto paper.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是压力把痕迹转移过去；义项由此分出压印的机器、从前动手的工人、拥有印刷机的商号，以及把影像压到纸上的冲印师。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a sheet sliding out of a machine, still warm from the ink.
core.cn: 核心意象：纸从机器里滑出来，还带着油墨的温热。

branches.cn: 纸页从嗡响的机器里滑出

branches.cn: 院子里摆着印刷机的作坊

branches.en: a darkroom tray holding a wet image
branches.cn: 暗房盘里浮着湿漉漉的影像

branches.en: the same pressure, once on paper and once on film
branches.cn: 同一种压力，一次压在纸上，一次压在胶片上

intro.en: The word is a Latin verb of pressing, its prefixed form, the French noun of an impression, the English verb, and the endings that name the doer and the trade.
intro.cn: 这个词由表示压的拉丁语动词、加前缀的形式、法语中表示印记的名词、英语动词，以及命名做者与行当的词尾共同支撑。

latinIntro.en: Latin premere and its prefixed form imprimere stand at the head of this family, so the pressing image is recorded in Latin even though the modern trade word was shaped in French and English.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 premere 及加前缀的 imprimere 处在这个词族的顶端，所以「压」的意象在拉丁语里就有记录，尽管现代行业词是在法语和英语里定型的。

core_image: 图书馆窗边低头翻书的人
scene: 图书馆的窗边，一个人低着头，一页页翻着手中的书。 The magazine invited its readers to send in questions.
sceneCN: 这里 reader 是「读者」（第 1 个义项：阅读书刊的人）；句意为这本杂志邀请读者寄来问题。画面里可留意：窗边的座位、低头翻书的人、摊开的书页。

pos.zh: 读者；读本；读取器；审稿人

read 加 -ing，指阅读、读数

senses.title: A person who reads
senses.definition: a person who reads books, magazines or other texts
senses.definitionCN: 阅读书籍、杂志或其他文本的人
senses.example: The magazine invited its readers to send in questions.
senses.exampleCN: 这本杂志邀请读者寄来问题。
senses.why: Reader is simply read plus the agent ending -er, so it names the one who performs the act of reading.
senses.whyCN: reader 就是 read 加施动词尾 -er，因此它命名的是执行阅读这一动作的人。

senses.title: A book for learning
senses.definition: a book containing texts chosen for learning a language or a subject
senses.definitionCN: 为学习语言或某科目而编选的文本汇编
senses.example: The class worked through a French reader.
senses.exampleCN: 全班学完了一本法语读本。
senses.why: A book made to be read by learners was called a reader, because the book itself is meant for reading practice.
senses.whyCN: 为学习者编的书被称为 reader，因为这本书本身就是供阅读练习用的。

senses.title: A device that reads data
senses.definition: a machine or device that reads information from cards, discs or codes
senses.definitionCN: 从卡片、光盘或代码中读取信息的机器或装置
senses.example: The guard swiped the card through the reader.
senses.exampleCN: 警卫把卡在读卡器上刷了一下。
senses.why: The agent ending was extended to machines, since a device that reads data performs the same act as a person reading it.
senses.whyCN: 施动词尾被扩展到机器，因为读取数据的装置与读数据的人执行同一个动作。

senses.title: A manuscript reviewer
senses.definition: a person employed to read and comment on manuscripts for a publisher
senses.definitionCN: 受雇为出版社阅读并评议稿件的人
senses.example: The manuscript was sent to an outside reader.
senses.exampleCN: 稿子被送给一位外审。
senses.why: In publishing, the person who reads a manuscript before it is accepted performs the act of reading as a job, hence the title reader.
senses.whyCN: 在出版业，接受前阅读稿子的人以阅读为职业，因此得到 reader 这个称号。

intro.en: Reader is formed in English from the verb read and the agent ending -er, and the verb itself goes back to Old English rædan.
intro.cn: reader 由英语动词 read 与施动词尾 -er 构成，而这个动词可追溯到古英语 rædan。

items.en: Old English had rædere for a reader or interpreter, formed from rædan, to read or explain.
items.cn: 古英语已有 rædere，指读者或解释者，由 rædan（阅读、解释）构成。

items.en: The ending -er marks the one who does an action, so read plus -er is the one who reads.
items.cn: 词尾 -er 标记执行动作的人，因此 read 加 -er 就是阅读的人。

items.en: Middle English reader kept the sense of a person who reads and began to name books meant for reading practice.
items.cn: 中古英语 reader 保留「阅读的人」之意，并开始指供阅读练习的书。

items.en: Modern use extended the word to machines that read data and to people paid to read manuscripts.
items.cn: 现代用法把这个词扩展到读取数据的机器，以及受雇阅读稿件的人。

items.en: Modern English uses reader for the person, the learning book, the device and the manuscript reviewer.
items.cn: 现代英语用 reader 指人、学习读本、读取器与审稿人。

note.en: The look-alike group gathers forms built on read; the near-meaning group gathers words for people who receive texts.
note.cn: 形近组收由 read 构成的形式；近义组收表示接收文本的人。

entries.definition: To understand written words.
The act of reading.
Easy to read.
The collective readers of a publication.
The people reached by a book, film or speech.
entries.definitionCN: 书、电影或演讲所触及的人群。

entries.definition: A person who pays to receive a publication.
entries.definitionCN: 付费订阅某出版物的人。

entries.definition: A person who watches something.
A person who is learning.

normalIntro.en: The word is read plus -er, and the ending has stretched from people to books, machines and manuscript reviewers.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是 read 加 -er，这个词尾已从人扩展到书、机器与审稿人。

normal.en: Reader is read plus -er, so it names whoever or whatever does the reading.
normal.cn: reader 是 read 加 -er，命名做阅读的人或物。

normal.en: A regular reader comes back to the same magazine issue after issue.
normal.cn: regular reader 一期又一期地回到同一本杂志。

normal.en: A graded reader is a book written at a controlled level for learners.
normal.cn: graded reader 是按受控难度为学习者写的书。

normal.en: A card reader reads the stripe on a card the way a person reads a page.
normal.cn: card reader 读卡片上的磁条，就像人读书页。

normal.en: Readership is the whole body of readers taken together.
normal.cn: readership 是把全体读者合在一起看。

abstract.en: A reader is not a passive receiver but a maker of meaning.
abstract.cn: 读者不是被动的接收者，而是意义的制作者。

abstract.en: Every text has as many readers as it has readings.
abstract.cn: 每个文本有多少种读法，就有多少个读者。

abstract.en: To be a good reader is to notice what the text leaves out.
abstract.cn: 做一个好读者，就是注意到文本省略了什么。

examples.en: The magazine invited its readers to send in questions.
examples.cn: 这本杂志邀请读者寄来问题。

examples.en: The class worked through a French reader.
examples.cn: 全班学完了一本法语读本。

examples.en: The guard swiped the card through the reader.
examples.cn: 警卫把卡在读卡器上刷了一下。

dict_mnemonic.text: 联想「窗边翻书的人」——read 加 -er 就是读者，记住 reader 是读者、读本。

root: 古英语 rædan（阅读、解释）→ 英语 read + 施动后缀 -er → reader；同族有 read、reading、readable、readership。

sensesIntro.en: The core is one who reads; the senses divide into a person, a learning book, a reading device, and a manuscript reviewer.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「阅读者」；义项分为人、学习读本、读取装置与审稿人。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a figure by a library window, head down, turning one page after another.
core.cn: 核心意象：图书馆窗边的一个人，低头一页页翻书。

branches.en: a reader by a library window
branches.cn: 图书馆窗边的读者

branches.en: a graded reader on a school desk
branches.cn: 课桌上的分级读本

branches.en: a card sliding through a reader
branches.cn: 穿过读取器的卡片

branches.en: a manuscript handed to an outside reader
branches.cn: 交给外审的稿子

branches.en: a person reading and a machine reading
branches.cn: 人阅读与机器读取

intro.en: The word is built in English from a native verb and a productive agent ending.
intro.cn: 这个词由本族动词与一个能产的施动词尾在英语中构成。

latinIntro.en: No reliable Latin source is recorded for this word.
latinIntro.cn: 这个词没有可靠的拉丁语来源记录。

definition_zh: 打架；搏斗；战斗；争吵；奋斗；对抗；战斗；斗志；吵架
definition_en: to use physical force against someone, or to struggle hard against something; also the act of fighting or a battle
core_image: 两人相向而立，拳头握紧，空气里满是紧绷的张力
scene: 放学后的巷口，两个男孩互相推搡，围观者越聚越多。 The two brothers fight over the remote control every evening.
sceneCN: 这里 fight 是动词，指「为争夺而争吵争抢」，对应第 5 个义项；句意为兄弟俩每晚都为遥控器争来争去。

pos.zh: 打架；搏斗；战斗；奋斗；争吵

derivatives.zh: 战士；斗士；战斗机（fight 加施动者后缀 -er，指战斗者或战斗机）
战斗；搏斗（fight 的动名词，指交战行为）
可争的；可搏斗的（fight 加 -able，罕见，指可一战之事）

senses.title: To use physical force
senses.definition: to hit or wrestle with someone physically
senses.definitionCN: 与人发生肢体上的击打或扭斗
senses.example: The boys fought in the schoolyard.
senses.exampleCN: 男孩们在校园里打了起来。
senses.why: Bodies first: the word begins with fists and muscle.
senses.whyCN: 身体为先：这个词始于拳头与肌肉。

senses.title: To take part in a war or battle
senses.definition: to take part in armed conflict as a soldier or group
senses.definitionCN: 作为士兵或团体参加武装冲突
senses.example: They fought bravely to defend the city.
senses.exampleCN: 他们为保卫城市而英勇作战。
senses.why: One-on-one force scaled up becomes armies and wars.
senses.whyCN: 一对一的力量放大后便是军队与战争。

senses.title: To struggle against something bad
senses.definition: to try hard to stop or defeat something harmful
senses.definitionCN: 努力阻止或击败有害之物
senses.example: Doctors fight the disease with new drugs.
senses.exampleCN: 医生用新药与疾病作斗争。
senses.why: The struggle turns inward or abstract: against illness, poverty, injustice.
senses.whyCN: 斗争转向内在或抽象：对抗疾病、贫困与不公。

senses.title: To compete hard for something
senses.definition: to compete with great effort to win something
senses.definitionCN: 为赢得某物而全力竞争
senses.example: She fought for every point in the final set.
senses.exampleCN: 决胜局她一分一分地拼。
senses.why: The arena need not be violent: sport and markets are fights too.
senses.whyCN: 竞技场未必暴力：赛场与市场同样是搏斗。

senses.title: To quarrel or argue
senses.definition: to have an angry argument with someone
senses.definitionCN: 与人发生激烈争执
senses.example: They fight about money all the time.
senses.exampleCN: 他们总为钱吵架。
senses.why: Words replace fists, but the force behind them stays the same.
senses.whyCN: 言语取代了拳头，但背后的力量并无二致。

intro.en: Fight is a Germanic strong verb whose old past tense fought survives intact, from a root that once meant to plait or tie a rope — force binding into struggle.
intro.cn: fight 是日耳曼强变化动词，古过去式 fought 完整保留；词根原义或为「编结、捆扎」，引申为缠斗。

items.en: A reconstructed root fekhtan meant 'to plait, twist together', which grew into fighting and fencing words.
items.cn: 一般认为，重构词根 fekhtan 意为「编结、绞缠」，衍生出搏斗与剑术一类词。

items.en: Old English feohtan meant 'to fight, contend', with past tense feaht.
items.cn: 古英语 feohtan 意为「搏斗、争斗」，过去式为 feaht。

items.en: Middle English fighten kept the strong past, spelled fought.
items.cn: 中古英语 fighten 保留强变化过去式，拼作 fought。

items.en: The noun fight grew beside the verb for battles, quarrels and struggles.
items.cn: 现代英语在动词旁发展出名词 fight，兼指战斗、争执与抗争。

items.en: Metaphors spread widely: fighting fit, a fight for survival, fighter jets.
items.cn: 比喻广泛传播：fighting fit、a fight for survival、fighter jets。

note.en: Look-alikes share the fi- shape or the old root; near-meaning words cover combat and struggle.
note.cn: 形近组共享 fi- 字形或古老词根；近义组覆盖搏斗与抗争。

entries.definition: the past of fight; same root, changed vowel
entries.definitionCN: fight 的过去式；同根变元音

entries.definition: sudden fear; one letter apart and unrelated
entries.definitionCN: 惊吓；仅一字母之差而词源无关

entries.definition: German Spruce tree; same old root for twisting wood
entries.definitionCN: 德语「云杉」；同一「绞缠」古根

entries.definition: a fight between armed groups
to try hard against difficulty
a noisy, rough fight

normalIntro.en: Five handles from the forms and the fixed phrases.
normalIntro.cn: 五个来自词形变化与固定短语的记忆抓手。

normal.en: fight / fought / fought: the vowel bends like a wrestler.
normal.cn: fight / fought / fought：元音像摔跤手一样弯折。

normal.en: fight for is the cause, fight against is the enemy.
normal.cn: fight for 指为之而战的信念，fight against 指对抗的敌人。

normal.en: fight back means to return the blow or refuse to give in.
normal.cn: fight back 表示还击或拒绝屈服。

normal.en: pick a fight means to start one on purpose.
normal.cn: pick a fight 表示故意挑衅开战。

normal.en: a fighter can be a person, a boxer, or a jet aircraft.
normal.cn: fighter 可以是人、拳击手，也可以是战斗机。

abstract.en: A fight is energy with an enemy attached to it.
abstract.cn: 搏斗是绑定了敌人的能量。

abstract.en: Some fights are won by refusing to fight.
abstract.cn: 有些战斗以拒绝出手取胜。

abstract.en: Quarrels are fights that lost their fists and kept their heat.
abstract.cn: 争吵是丢了拳头、留下火气的搏斗。

examples.en: Rescuers fought the fire through the night.
examples.cn: 救援人员彻夜与大火搏斗。

examples.en: The two teams fought hard for the championship.
examples.cn: 两队为冠军展开激烈争夺。

examples.en: Their fight over the family business lasted years.
examples.cn: 他们为家族生意之争持续了多年。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「法伊特」—— 出手时先喊一声「法伊特」，像擂台开打 → fight 打架、战斗

root: 出自古英语 feohtan「搏斗」，上溯日耳曼词根 fekhtan（一般认为是「编结、绞缠」，引申为缠斗）；德语 fechten「击剑」同源。

sensesIntro.en: From fists outward to armies, struggles against harm, hard competition and angry words.
sensesIntro.cn: 从拳头出发，扩展到军队作战、对抗恶疾、激烈竞争与争吵。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: two bodies pushing against each other with everything they have.
core.cn: 核心意象：两具身体倾尽全力彼此相抗。

branches.en: THE BLOWS: physical fighting.
branches.cn: 拳脚：身体的搏斗。

branches.en: THE WAR: battle between groups.
branches.cn: 战争：群体之间的交战。

branches.en: THE CAUSE: struggle against harm.
branches.cn: 抗争：对抗有害之事。

branches.en: THE RACE: hard competition to win.
branches.cn: 竞争：为胜利全力以赴。

branches.en: THE WORDS: quarrels without fists.
branches.cn: 口角：不动拳头的争执。

intro.en: Fight forms compounds readily: fighter, firefight, fight back and more.
intro.cn: fight 极易构成复合词：fighter、firefight、fight back 等。

latinIntro.en: Latin fights with pugnare and bellum, different roots, so fight has no Latin siblings.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 pugnare 与 bellum 表战斗，词根不同，故 fight 无拉丁同族词。

items.example: A brief firefight shook the valley.
The trapped miners fought back tears.

items.meaning: to march on foot; shares the old root family
the instinct to resist or flee
items.example: The fight or flight response kicked in.

definition_zh: 欢迎；迎接；受欢迎的；可随意使用的
definition_en: to greet someone in a friendly way, and to be gladly received or freely allowed
core_image: 院门被推开，主人快步迎出来，伸手接过客人的行李
scene: 第一次到同学家，他母亲在门口等着，接过包，说路上辛苦了，快进来。 His mother met me at the door, took my bag and welcomed me inside.
sceneCN: 这里 welcome 是「欢迎」（第 1 个义项：友善地迎接某人）；句意为他母亲在门口接了我，接过包把我迎进屋。推门而出、伸手接手提行李的主人就是这个词的印象。

pos.zh: 受欢迎的；可随意使用的

collocations.zh: 欢迎来到我们这座城市

derivatives.zh: 热情好客的
门口的踏垫
不受欢迎的
受欢迎地
迎接者

senses.title: To greet someone gladly
senses.definition: to meet a person in a friendly way and show that one is glad they came
senses.definitionCN: 友善地迎接某人，并表现出对他们的到来感到高兴
senses.example: They welcomed the guests at the gate with tea.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在门口用茶迎接客人。
senses.why: This is the core sense: the friendly meeting at arrival.
senses.whyCN: 这是核心义：到访时友善的迎接。

senses.title: To be glad to accept
senses.definition: to receive an idea, a change or a gift with pleasure
senses.definitionCN: 愉快地接受某个想法、变化或礼物
senses.example: We welcome any suggestions for the new plan.
senses.exampleCN: 我们乐于接受对新计划的任何建议。
senses.why: A change can be greeted as a guest is, so the verb spreads to things.
senses.whyCN: 变化也能像客人一样被迎进来，于是动词扩展到事物。

senses.title: Received with pleasure
senses.definition: of news or events, gladly received
senses.definitionCN: 指消息或事件令人高兴
senses.example: The rain was welcome after a month of heat.
senses.exampleCN: 热了一个月之后，这场雨很受欢迎。
senses.why: The adjective describes what people would be glad to greet.
senses.whyCN: 形容词描述人们乐于迎接的东西。

senses.title: Freely permitted to use
senses.titleCN: 可随意使用的；受欢迎的（人）
senses.definition: of a person, allowed to do or take something without asking
senses.definitionCN: 指人无需请示即可使用或取用
senses.example: You are welcome to stay for dinner.
senses.exampleCN: 欢迎你留下吃晚饭。
senses.why: To be welcome somewhere is to be free of the usual barrier.
senses.whyCN: 在某处受欢迎，就是不受通常的界限阻挡。

senses.title: A greeting of arrival
senses.definition: the act of greeting, usually warm, in the noun form
senses.definitionCN: 名词形式，带来暖意的迎接行为
senses.example: They gave us a warm welcome at the station.
senses.exampleCN: 他们在车站给了我们热烈的欢迎。
senses.why: The friendly meeting at the gate turned into a noun, so it became a thing one gives.
senses.whyCN: 门口那场友善的相见转为名词，于是成了一份可以送出的东西。

senses.title: A polite reply
senses.definition: a fixed reply to thanks, meaning there is no need to thank
senses.definitionCN: 对道谢的固定回答，意为不必谢
senses.example: “Thank you.” “You’re welcome.”
senses.exampleCN: “谢谢。”“不用谢。”
senses.why: The reply says the favour was freely given, so no debt remains.
senses.whyCN: 这句答语表示这份好意是白送的，因此不欠什么。

intro.en: Welcome is Old English wilcuma, a compound of will and come, meaning a guest whose coming is wished for.
intro.cn: welcome 是古英语 wilcuma，由 will 与 come 复合而成，意为「来得合人心愿的客人」。

items.en: Wilcuma named a desired guest, someone whose arrival pleased the host.
items.cn: wilcuma 指备受期盼的客人，其到来使主人高兴。

items.en: The first element is will, the wish, and the second is come, so the word literally means wished-coming.
items.cn: 第一部分是 will（意愿），第二部分是 come，字面即「如人所愿的到来」。

items.en: The noun was reshaped under the influence of French bienvenu and gave a verb welcome.
items.cn: 名词受法语 bienvenu 影响而变形，并衍生出动词 welcome。

items.en: The adjective sense of freely allowed appeared, as in you are welcome to try.
items.cn: 形容词「可随意」的义项出现，如 you are welcome to try。

items.en: You are welcome as a reply to thanks is recorded from the nineteenth century.
items.cn: 「不用谢」这一答语自十九世纪有记录。

note.en: The first group shares the welcome shape, the second gives the words used at a greeting.
note.cn: 第一组与 welcome 形近同族，第二组是迎接时的近义词。

entries.definition: Friendly to guests, or the act of greeting.
Not wanted or gladly received.
One who greets others.
The Old English ancestor, a wished-for guest.
entries.definitionCN: 古英语本源：受期盼的客人

entries.definition: To say hello to someone in a friendly way.
To meet and admit a guest, often formally.
Friendly care shown to guests.
To take what is offered.

normalIntro.en: Say the word slowly: will plus come, a coming that someone wishes for.
normalIntro.cn: 慢慢念这个词：will 加 come，一次有人盼望的到来。

normal.en: Welcome is verb, adjective and noun all at once.
normal.cn: welcome 可作动词、形容词和名词。

normal.en: You are welcome is the fixed reply to thanks.
normal.cn: You are welcome 是对道谢的固定回答。

normal.en: A warm welcome is the noun after an adjective.
normal.cn: a warm welcome 是形容词加名词。

normal.en: Unwelcome news is news nobody wanted.
normal.cn: unwelcome news 是没人想要的消息。

normal.en: Make someone welcome means put them at ease.
normal.cn: make someone welcome 是让某人自在。

abstract.en: Picture a gate swung open from inside.
abstract.cn: 想门从里面被推开。

abstract.en: Feel a bag lifted out of your hand.
abstract.cn: 感受手里的包被接走。

abstract.en: Hear the door close warmly behind you.
abstract.cn: 听门在身后温和地关上。

examples.en: They welcomed us with tea and fruit.
examples.cn: 他们用茶和水果欢迎我们。

examples.en: Your comments are welcome at any time.
examples.cn: 随时欢迎您提出意见。

examples.en: “Thanks for the lift.” “You’re welcome.”
examples.cn: “谢谢你载我一程。”“不客气。”

dict_mnemonic.text: 「维尔康」——维尔康先生每到门口就说：来得好，欢迎进屋。

root: 古英语 wilcuma（will 意愿 + cuma 来者，即受期盼的客人）→ 中古英语受法语 bienvenu 影响成 welcome。

sensesIntro.en: The word starts as a wished-for arrival, becomes the act of greeting, then any glad acceptance and even the answer to thanks.
sensesIntro.cn: 这个词从「如人所愿的到来」出发，成为迎接的行为，再扩展到任何乐意的接受，乃至道谢的答语。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a host taking a guest’s bag at the gate.
core.cn: 核心意象：主人在门口接过客人的包。

branches.en: The greeting branch: guests met at the gate and a warm welcome.
branches.cn: 迎接分支：门口迎客与热烈欢迎。

branches.en: The acceptance branch: suggestions and rain both welcome.
branches.cn: 接受分支：建议与雨都受欢迎。

branches.en: The permission branch: you are welcome to stay.
branches.cn: 许可分支：欢迎你留下。

branches.en: The reply branch: you’re welcome.
branches.cn: 答语分支：不用谢。

branches.en: The host and the permission branch: one opens a door, the other a choice.
branches.cn: 主人分支与许可分支：一个开门，一个放行。

intro.en: Welcome is a very old compound that can now be a verb, an adjective or a noun.
intro.cn: welcome 是很古老的复合词，如今可作动词、形容词或名词。

latinIntro.en: Latin used gratus and acceptare for being welcome, and the table gives those cousins.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语用 gratus 与 acceptare 表示受欢迎与被接受，拉丁表给出这些亲族词。

definition_zh: 圆；圆圈；圈子；循环；盘旋
definition_en: a perfectly round flat shape; a group of people with shared interests; to move around something
core_image: 一根从起点绕回起点的封闭曲线
scene: 体育课上，大家手拉手围成一团做游戏。 We formed a circle and passed the ball.
sceneCN: 这里 circle 是「圆圈」（第 1 个义项：完美的圆形）；句意是我们围成一个圈传球。

derivatives.zh: 由 circle 加后缀 -ar 构成，义为「圆形的；循环的」
由 circle 加后缀 -ate 构成，义为「循环；流通」
由拉丁词根构成的相关词，义为「圆周」
加前缀 en- 构成，义为「环绕；包围」

senses.title: A perfectly round shape
senses.definition: a closed curve where every point is equally far from the centre
senses.definitionCN: 各点到中心等距的封闭曲线
senses.example: She drew a big circle on the paper.
senses.exampleCN: 她在纸上画了一个大圆。
senses.why: The geometry sense names the basic shape.
senses.whyCN: 几何义项命名了这个基本图形。

senses.title: A group of people sharing something
senses.definition: a group of people connected by shared interests or work
senses.definitionCN: 因共同兴趣或职业而联系的一群人
senses.example: He is popular in the music circle.
senses.exampleCN: 他在音乐圈很受欢迎。
senses.why: People sitting in a circle become the circle of people.
senses.whyCN: 围坐成圈的一群人便成了「圈子」。

senses.title: To move around something
senses.definition: to fly or move round and round something
senses.definitionCN: 围着某物不停地转
senses.example: The bird circled above the field.
senses.exampleCN: 鸟儿在田野上空盘旋。
senses.why: The noun shape turns into the motion tracing it.
senses.whyCN: 名词图形转化为描绘图形的运动。

senses.title: A series repeating regularly
senses.definition: a repeating series of events that ends where it began
senses.definitionCN: 首尾相接、周而复始的一系列事件
senses.example: Seasons move in a circle year after year.
senses.exampleCN: 四季年年循环往复。
senses.why: A closed curve has no ends, like events that repeat.
senses.whyCN: 封闭曲线没有起点终点，恰如循环往复的事情。

intro.en: Circle came from Greek through Latin and Old French into English.
intro.cn: circle 从希腊语经拉丁语和古法语进入英语。

items.en: Greek kirkos or krikos named a ring or hoop.
items.cn: 希腊语 kirkos 或 krikos 指环、箍。

items.en: Latin borrowed it as circus, meaning a ring or circle.
items.cn: 拉丁语借入为 circus，义为环、圆形场地。

items.en: Old French turned it into cercle, keeping the round sense.
items.cn: 古法语演变为 cercle，保留圆形义。

items.en: Middle English took it as cercle around the fourteenth century.
items.cn: 约十四世纪中古英语借入 cercle。

items.en: Modern English fixed the spelling as circle and added verb uses.
items.cn: 现代英语定型为 circle，并发展出动词用法。

note.en: The first group gathers round-shape words; the second gathers look-alikes.
note.cn: 第一组收圆形类词，第二组收形近词。

entries.definition: A show with clowns and acrobats.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「马戏团」，同出拉丁语 circus（环场）。

entries.definition: Shaped like a circle.
entries.definitionCN: 形容词，义为「圆形的」，是 circle 的派生词。

entries.definition: A repeating series or a bicycle.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「循环；自行车」，词形相近、同指环转。

entries.definition: A circle of metal or people.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「环；戒指；围成一圈的人」。

entries.definition: A round solid shape like a ball.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「球体」，圆形的立体版。

entries.definition: The path of circling a star or planet.
entries.definitionCN: 名词，义为「轨道」，围绕转动的路径。

normalIntro.en: Remember circle by its root family of roundness.
normalIntro.cn: 通过「圆形」词族记忆 circle。

normal.en: circus began as a ring-shaped arena.
normal.cn: circum 最初指环形竞技场。

normal.en: circulate means to move round like a circle.
normal.cn: circulate 指像圆一样循环流动。

normal.en: circle of friends is a common phrase.
normal.cn: circle of friends 是常见搭配。

normal.en: draw a circle starts geometry homework.
normal.cn: 几何作业常从画圆开始。

normal.en: the verb circle means to go round.
normal.cn: 动词 circle 表示环绕。

abstract.en: Trace a curve that meets its own tail.
abstract.cn: 描绘一条首尾相接的曲线。

abstract.en: Watch a hawk hanging on still air in loops.
abstract.cn: 看鹰在静空中一圈圈盘旋。

abstract.en: Feel friends closing a ring with joined hands.
abstract.cn: 感受朋友们手拉手围成的圆环。

examples.en: The teacher asked us to circle the right answer.
examples.cn: 老师让我们把正确答案圈出来。

examples.en: A plane circled over the airport before landing.
examples.cn: 飞机降落前在机场上空盘旋。

examples.en: The children sat in a circle to sing.
examples.cn: 孩子们围坐成一圈唱歌。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑟扣」——瑟瑟的风把纸片吹成一个扣住的圆圈。

root: 希腊语 kirkos（环）→ 拉丁语 circus（环形场地）→ 古法语 cercle → 中古英语 cercle → 现代英语 circle；同根词有 circus（马戏团）、circular（圆形的）、circulate（循环）。

sensesIntro.en: Circle runs from the round shape to human groups, circling motion and repeating cycles.
sensesIntro.cn: circle 从圆形出发，延伸到人群圈子、环绕运动和循环周期。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a curve that returns to its own start
core.cn: 核心意象：绕回起点的封闭曲线

branches.en: The geometric shape
branches.cn: 几何圆形

branches.en: A social group
branches.cn: 社交圈子

branches.en: Motion around a centre
branches.cn: 绕心运动

branches.en: Events that repeat
branches.cn: 周而复始的事件

branches.en: Drawing a round mark
branches.cn: 画出圈形记号

intro.en: The root circ- or circ- family means ring and turn.
intro.cn: 词根 circ- 家族表示「环、转」。

latinIntro.en: Latin circus is the parent of many English circle words.
latinIntro.cn: 拉丁语 circus 是许多英语环形词的母体。

items.example: The letter O is a circle.
A circular track surrounds the field.
Measure the circumference of the wheel.
We watched a circus last week.
items.exampleCN: 上周我们看了马戏表演。

items.example: The washing cycle takes an hour.

definition_zh: 忘记；忘掉；忘了带；不再想
definition_en: to fail to remember or keep in mind; to fail to bring something
core_image: 记忆像手里的沙子：一松手就漏光了
scene: 出门前，小明找了半天书包，才发现作业本还摊在书桌上。 He was in such a hurry that he forgot to bring his homework.
sceneCN: 这里 forget 是「忘了做某事」（第 1 个义项：没有记住去做）；小明因为匆忙，脑子里根本没记住要带作业这件事。

collocations.zh: 忘记去做某事（事还没做）
忘记曾经做过某事（事已做过）

derivatives.zh: forget 加形容词后缀 -ful，义为「健忘的；常忘事的」
forgetful 的副词形式，义为「健忘地；常忘事地」
forgetful 的名词形式，义为「健忘；疏忽」
加否定前缀 un-，义为「难忘的；无法忘怀的」

senses.title: To fail to remember information or an action
senses.definition: to be unable to recall a fact, or to fail to remember to do something
senses.definitionCN: 想不起某件事，或没有记住要去做某事。
senses.example: I forgot her phone number, so I could not call her.
senses.exampleCN: 我忘了她的电话号码，所以没法给她打电话。
senses.why: The prefix for- means away, so forgetting is memory that falls away from the mind.
senses.whyCN: 前缀 for- 表示「离开」，所以忘记就是记忆从头脑中脱落。

senses.title: To fail to bring or take something
senses.definition: to fail to bring an object you intended to bring
senses.definitionCN: 本来打算带的东西，结果没有带。
senses.example: She forgot her umbrella on the train.
senses.exampleCN: 她把伞忘在火车上了。
senses.why: The mental slip extends to physical objects left behind.
senses.whyCN: 头脑中的疏忽延伸到实物：该带的东西被落下了。

senses.title: To stop thinking or caring about something
senses.definition: to put something out of your mind deliberately
senses.definitionCN: 有意把某事从心里放下，不再纠缠。
senses.example: Forget the argument and enjoy the holiday.
senses.exampleCN: 别再想那场争吵，好好享受假期吧。
senses.why: Forgetting is also an act of letting go, not just a failure of memory.
senses.whyCN: 忘记不只是记忆失败，也可以是一种主动的放下。

intro.en: Forget is an Old English compound whose parts still mean exactly what they suggest.
intro.cn: forget 是一个古英语复合词，其组成部分的含义至今与直觉一致。

items.en: The verb getan meant 'to grasp, seize, obtain', the ancestor of modern get.
items.cn: 古英语动词 getan 意为「抓住、获得」，是现代 get 的祖先。

items.en: The prefix for- meant 'away, off', turning 'grasp' into 'lose one's grip'.
items.cn: 前缀 for- 意为「离开、脱落」，把「抓住」变成「抓不住」。

items.en: Forgietan therefore meant 'to lose hold of the mind', that is, to lose a memory.
items.cn: forgietan 因此意为「在头脑中失去持有」，也就是丢失一段记忆。

items.en: The word continued as forgetten, with the past forms forgot and forgotten settling down.
items.cn: 该词在中古英语中写作 forgetten，过去式 forgot 与过去分词 forgotten 逐渐定型。

items.en: The deliberate sense 'stop caring' and the derived word unforgettable developed in later centuries.
items.cn: 「不再想」的主动义项和派生词 unforgettable 在后世逐渐发展出来。

note.en: Words shaped like forget and words about losing memory.
note.cn: 与 forget 形近的词以及表示记忆丢失的词。

entries.definition: to stop being angry at someone; shares the for- prefix meaning 'away'
entries.definitionCN: 原谅；与 forget 共用表示「离开」的前缀 for-，同属古英语 for- 动词家族。

entries.definition: to abandon someone or something; another for- verb of Old English origin
entries.definitionCN: 抛弃；同样是带 for- 前缀的古英语动词，语义核心是「舍弃」。

entries.definition: the present participle of forget itself
entries.definitionCN: forget 的现在分词；提醒学习者本词的 -tt- 双写规律。

entries.definition: to leave out, especially from a list or text
entries.definitionCN: 省略、遗漏；比 forget 更书面，强调有意或无意地漏掉。

entries.definition: to fail to notice something
entries.definitionCN: 忽视、没注意到；强调观察层面的疏漏。

entries.definition: to fail to care for something properly
entries.definitionCN: 疏于照顾、忽视；强调该尽的责任没有尽到。

normalIntro.en: Five hooks built on the for- + get structure of forget.
normalIntro.cn: 基于 forget 的 for- + get 结构的五条记忆钩子。

normal.en: Break forget into for + get: you did not get the memory, so it is gone.
normal.cn: 拆成 for + get：「没拿到」记忆，自然就忘了。

normal.en: The for- prefix also appears in forgive and forsake: it marks letting go.
normal.cn: for- 前缀也出现在 forgive、forsake 中：都表示「放手、舍弃」。

normal.en: Use the contrast: remember to remember, forget to forget.
normal.cn: 用对反差记：remember 是「再抓一次」，forget 是「没抓住」。

normal.en: Note the double t in forgetting: short vowel before stress doubles.
normal.cn: 注意 forgetting 中 t 双写：重读闭音节前辅音字母要双写。

normal.en: Learn the pair 'forget to do' (not done) versus 'forget doing' (already done).
normal.cn: 记住 forget to do（还没做）与 forget doing（已做过）的差别。

abstract.en: Picture sand slipping through open fingers.
abstract.cn: 想象沙子从张开的手指间漏下去。

abstract.en: Picture a balloon flying away from your hand.
abstract.cn: 想象一个气球从你手中飞走。

abstract.en: Picture words on a whiteboard being wiped clean.
abstract.cn: 想象白板上的字被擦得一干二净。

examples.en: Do not forget to lock the door when you leave.
examples.cn: 离开时别忘了锁门。

examples.en: He forgot that the meeting had been moved to Friday.
examples.cn: 他忘了会议已改到周五。

examples.en: I will never forget the kindness my teacher showed me.
examples.cn: 我永远不会忘记老师对我的好。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「佛给特」——连佛祖都特别给不了的记忆，说明你彻底忘了：forget 就是「抓不住」的记忆。

root: forget 来自古英语 forgietan：for-（偏离、失去）+ getan（抓住、获得）。字面义「失去持有」，即「丢失记忆」。与 forgive、forsake 同属古英语 for- 动词家族，都表示「放手」类动作。

sensesIntro.en: Forget moves from failed memory to abandoned objects to deliberate letting go.
sensesIntro.cn: forget 从「记忆失败」延伸到「该带的没带」，再到主动的「放下、不再想」。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a hand that fails to hold what it grasped
core.cn: 核心意象：一只抓不住东西的手

branches.en: A fact or action slips out of memory
branches.cn: 事实或要做的事从记忆中滑走

branches.en: Failure to remember an intended action
branches.cn: 没记住本来打算做的事

branches.en: The mental slip leaves a physical object behind
branches.cn: 头脑的疏忽让实物被落下

branches.en: Releasing a memory on purpose to feel lighter
branches.cn: 主动松开一段记忆，让心变轻松

branches.en: One image covers both losing and letting go
branches.cn: 同一个意象覆盖「无意丢失」与「有意放下」两端

intro.en: Forget shows the Old English for- prefix, which turns positive verbs into losing verbs.
intro.cn: forget 展示了古英语 for- 前缀：它把「得到类」动词变成「失去类」动词。

latinIntro.en: The for- family is Germanic, not Latin, so the comparison words below are native English verbs.
latinIntro.cn: for- 词族是日耳曼来源而非拉丁来源，因此对照词都选英语本土动词。

items.example: Forsake means to leave someone away from you.
items.exampleCN: forsake 中 for- 表示「离开」。

items.example: You get a letter from a friend.

items.meaning: to give away a debt of anger
items.example: She forgave her brother at once.
items.exampleCN: forgive 与 forget 同构：for- + 动词。

items.example: He would never forsake his friends.
Grandpa is a bit forgetful these days.
items.exampleCN: 形容词后缀 -ful 在此表「充满」。
双重后缀叠加：un- 否定 + -able 可被。

items.example: The old gate had been forgotten for years.

items.meaningCN: 记住；想起（拉丁来源的反义词）
items.exampleCN: remember 与 forget 构成核心反义对。

definition_zh: 听见；听到；听说
definition_en: to notice sounds with your ears; to be told about something
core_image: 耳朵竖起的雷达：声波撞进来就被捕捉
scene: 深夜的走廊很静，隔壁房间钢琴声一点点飘过来。 She stopped to hear the music coming from the next room.
sceneCN: 这里 hear 是「听见」（第 1 个义项：用耳朵察觉声音）；她停下脚步捕捉琴声，hear 强调声音进入耳朵的结果。

derivatives.zh: 听力；听觉，由 hear 加后缀 -ing 构成
听者，与 hear 同义场的 listen 加后缀构成
听众，拉丁同义源词，与 hear 意义对应

senses.title: To notice sound with the ears
senses.definition: to become aware of a sound through the ears
senses.definitionCN: 通过耳朵察觉声音
senses.example: I can hear birds singing outside the window.
senses.exampleCN: 我能听见窗外鸟儿在唱歌。
senses.why: The ear works like a receiver catching sound waves, so hear names the act of catching a sound.
senses.whyCN: 耳朵像接收声波的雷达，hear 命名的就是捕捉到声音这个动作。

senses.title: To listen and pay attention
senses.definition: to listen carefully to what someone says
senses.definitionCN: 认真听某人说话
senses.example: The judge heard both sides before deciding.
senses.exampleCN: 法官听取双方陈述后才做决定。
senses.why: Catching a sound becomes catching someone's words and arguments, so hear extends to formal listening.
senses.whyCN: 捕捉声音延伸为捕捉言语与论点，hear 由此覆盖正式的听取场合。

senses.title: To be told or learn about
senses.definition: to be told about or learn about something
senses.definitionCN: 被告知或了解到某事
senses.example: Have you heard the news about the school trip?
senses.exampleCN: 你听说学校旅行了吗？
senses.why: Sound carries information, so hearing becomes receiving news through talk.
senses.whyCN: 声音承载信息，听见便延伸为经由言谈接收消息。

intro.en: Hear is an old Germanic verb tied to the ear family of words.
intro.cn: hear 是古老的日耳曼动词，与 ear 词族相关联。

items.en: Old English had heran or hieran, meaning to hear and to obey.
items.cn: 古英语作 heran 或 hieran，意为「听见、听从」。

items.en: It comes from the Germanic root *hauzjan, related to the word for ear.
items.cn: 它来自日耳曼词根 *hauzjan，与「耳朵」一词相关。

items.en: Old Norse heyra is a close relative with the same meaning.
items.cn: 古诺斯语 heyra 是同义的近亲词。

items.en: In Middle English, hear and listen settled into their modern roles: catch and attend.
items.cn: 中古英语里 hear 与 listen 分工定型：前者表示听见，后者表示倾听。

items.en: Modern English kept the irregular past heard and added phrases like hear from and hear of.
items.cn: 现代英语保留了不规则过去式 heard，并发展出 hear from、hear of 等短语。

note.en: Look-alikes and hearing neighbours.
note.cn: hear 的形近词与听觉近邻。

entries.definition: past form of hear
entries.definitionCN: hear 的过去式，同根变形

entries.definition: the organ that pumps blood
entries.definitionCN: 心脏，拼写相近但词源不同

entries.definition: the organ of hearing
entries.definitionCN: 耳朵，同族词，与 hear 同源

entries.definition: to pay attention to sound
to hear by accident
what is heard
entries.definitionCN: 声音，作为 hear 的对象

normalIntro.en: Five ways to fix hear in memory.
normalIntro.cn: 五个方式把 hear 记牢。

normal.en: hear vs listen
normal.cn: 对比「hear vs listen」：hear 是结果，listen 是主动动作。

normal.en: hear from
normal.cn: 短语「hear from」（收到消息）是最常见搭配之一。

normal.en: irregular heard
normal.cn: 过去式 heard 不加 -ed，读音也变。

normal.en: hear of and hear about
normal.cn: 「hear of / hear about」都表示听说，程度略有不同。

normal.en: ear inside hear
normal.cn: hear 里藏着 ear：耳朵在词中，意义也在耳朵。

abstract.en: Picture radar ears catching sound waves.
abstract.cn: 想象雷达般的耳朵捕捉声波：hear 就是声波被接收的瞬间。

abstract.en: Let the sound turn into news in your mind.
abstract.cn: 让声音在心里变成消息：听见即得知。

abstract.en: Sit in court and take in both sides.
abstract.cn: 坐在法庭上听取双方陈词：hear 的庄重用法。

examples.en: Did you hear that strange sound last night?
examples.cn: 昨晚你听见那个奇怪的声音了吗？

examples.en: I heard from my old friend after five years.
examples.cn: 五年后我收到了老朋友的消息。

examples.en: The audience heard the singer perform three songs.
examples.cn: 听众听了歌手演唱三首歌。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「希尔」——爬山到山顶「希尔」风声很大，你hear（听见）了呼呼的风。

root: hear 来自古英语 heran/hieran，源自日耳曼词根 *hauzjan（与 ear「耳」同族），古诺斯语 heyra 为近亲。古英语兼有「听从」义，现代英语里 hear 表示听见的结果，listen 表示倾听的过程。

sensesIntro.en: From catching sounds to taking in words and news.
sensesIntro.cn: 从捕捉声音到接收话语与消息。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: radar ears catching sound waves
core.cn: 核心意象：雷达般的耳朵捕捉声波

branches.en: Sounds that reach the ear
branches.cn: 进入耳朵的声音

branches.en: Words listened to carefully

definition_zh: 厘米（米的百分之一）
definition_en: a unit of length equal to one hundredth of a metre
core_image: 一把直尺上一格一格的小刻度
scene: 裁缝铺里，师傅用软尺仔细量我的手臂长度。 The tailor measured my arm and wrote down the centimetre.
sceneCN: 这里 centimetre 是「厘米」（第 1 个义项：米的百分之一）；句意是裁缝量我的手臂并记下厘米数。

derivatives.zh: 本词的基准单位，义为「米」
由 milli- 加 metre 构成，义为「毫米」

senses.title: A unit of length
senses.definition: a measure of length; one hundred centimetres make one metre
senses.definitionCN: 长度单位，一百厘米等于一米
senses.example: The fish was fifteen centimetres long.
senses.exampleCN: 那条鱼有十五厘米长。
senses.why: The word builds the metre into a hundred small pieces, centi- plus metre.
senses.whyCN: 这个词把米分成一百小份：centi-（百分之一）加 metre（米）。

senses.title: A small distance
senses.definition: a short distance measured in this unit, often in descriptions
senses.definitionCN: 用这个单位度量的短距离，常用于描写
senses.example: Move the chair a centimetre to the left.
senses.exampleCN: 把椅子向左挪一厘米。
senses.why: Because it is such a small step, writers use it for tiny movements.
senses.whyCN: 由于它是一小步，人们用它描写极微小的移动。

intro.en: The word is pure French science-building: centi- plus metre.
intro.cn: 这个词是法国科学造词的产物：centi- 加 metre。

items.en: Latin centum means a hundred, and centi- became the prefix for one hundredth.
items.cn: 拉丁语 centum 意为「一百」，centi- 成为「百分之一」的前缀。

items.en: Greek metron means a measure.
items.cn: 希腊语 metron 意为「测量」。

items.en: In 1795 French scientists created the metric system and coined centimetre.
items.cn: 一七九五年，法国科学家创立公制，造出 centimetre 一词。

items.en: English took the word from French, keeping the French spelling -re in Britain.
items.cn: 英语从法语借入该词，英国保留法语拼法 -re。

items.en: American English respells it centimeter, with the same sound.
items.cn: 美式英语把它拼作 centimeter，读音相同。

note.en: This family is all about measuring, from tiny to huge.
note.cn: 这一家族都是度量单位，从极小到极大。

one thousand metres

normal.en: centi- = one hundredth of something.
normal.cn: centi- 表示某物的百分之一。

normal.en: metre = the base unit of length.

normal.en: centi- + metre = one hundredth of a metre.

normal.en: Family words: millimetre, kilometre, centimetre.

normal.en: A fingernail is about one centimetre wide.
normal.cn: 指甲盖大约一厘米宽。

abstract.en: Picture a ruler where each small step is a centimetre.
abstract.cn: 想象一把直尺，每一小格就是一厘米。

abstract.en: Picture a snowfall piling up a few centimetres overnight.
abstract.cn: 想象一夜之间积雪堆了几厘米。

abstract.en: Picture a plant growing one centimetre every week on the windowsill.
abstract.cn: 想象窗台上的植物每周长高一厘米。

examples.en: The bridge is only thirty centimetres above the water.
examples.cn: 这座桥离水面只有三十厘米。

examples.en: Our maths book says one metre equals one hundred centimetres.
examples.cn: 数学书上说一米等于一百厘米。

examples.en: The rabbit hopped a few centimetres closer to the carrot.
examples.cn: 兔子朝胡萝卜又跳近了几厘米。

sensesIntro.en: A small step on the ruler and in space.

definition_zh: 修理；修补；修复；维修工作
definition_en: to mend something broken or damaged so that it works or looks right again
core_image: 把断开的零件重新对齐、拧紧，机器重新转了起来
scene: 老式收音机不出声了，师傅打开后盖换掉一根线，它重新唱了起来。 The shop repaired her old radio in a single afternoon.
sceneCN: 这里 repair 是「修理」（第 1 个义项：把损坏的东西恢复到可用状态）；句意：这家店一个下午就修好了她的旧收音机。

derivatives.zh: 修理者
可修复的
无法修复的

senses.title: To fix something broken
senses.definition: to mend a broken or damaged object so that it can be used again
senses.definitionCN: 修补破损的东西，使其能够重新使用
senses.example: He repaired the chair with glue and a new screw.
senses.exampleCN: 他用胶水和一颗新螺丝修好了椅子。
senses.why: The Latin verb reparare means to make ready again, so the core action is restoring an object to working order.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 reparare 意为「重新准备好」，所以核心动作是把物件恢复到可用的状态。

senses.title: The work of mending
senses.definition: the work or act of mending something, or the state of being mended
senses.definitionCN: 修补某物的动作或工作，也指被修好的状态
senses.example: The bridge is closed for repair.
senses.exampleCN: 这座桥因为维修而关闭。
senses.why: The noun simply names the action that the verb describes.
senses.whyCN: 名词义项只是给动词所描述的动作一个名称。

senses.title: To restore a relationship
senses.definition: to do something that makes a damaged relationship or situation healthy again
senses.definitionCN: 采取措施，使受损的关系或局面恢复健康
senses.example: The two countries worked hard to repair their friendship.
senses.exampleCN: 两国努力修复彼此的友谊。
senses.why: The image of putting broken parts back together extends from objects to trust and relations.
senses.whyCN: 把破损零件重新拼好的画面，从物件延伸到信任与关系。

intro.en: Repair comes through Old French from Latin reparare, built from re-, again, and parare, to prepare.
intro.cn: repair 经由古法语来自拉丁语 reparare，由 re-（再次）与 parare（准备）构成。

items.en: Parare means to prepare, make ready, or arrange.
items.cn: parare 意为准备、使就绪或安排。

items.en: Reparare adds re-, again, and so means to make ready once more.
items.cn: reparare 加上 re-（再次），意为「重新使就绪」。

items.en: The word is used for restoring buildings, bodies, and broken tools.
items.cn: 这个词被用于修复建筑、身体和破损的工具。

items.en: Old French reparer keeps the sense of mending and putting right.
items.cn: 古法语 reparer 保留了「修补、纠正」的意思。

items.en: Middle English repair covers both fixing objects and restoring a damaged name.
items.cn: 中古英语 repair 既能指修物件，也能指修复受损的名声。

items.en: Modern English adds the noun use for the work and the condition of being mended.
items.cn: 现代英语又增加了名词用法，指维修工作以及被修好的状态。

note.en: Repair belongs to a small family of making broken things whole, and it is close to everyday words for fixing.
note.cn: repair 属于「让破损之物复原」的小词族，与日常表示修理的词很接近。

entries.definition: able to be repaired
impossible to repair or put right
a person whose job is to repair machines
to repair something that is torn or broken
to make something work again
to bring something back to its earlier good condition
the work of keeping something in good condition

normalIntro.en: Repair can be split into re- and pair, and the pair image works well because repair puts two broken parts back together.
normalIntro.cn: repair 可以拆成 re- 与 pair，而「配对」的画面很好用，因为修理就是把两个断开的部件重新配在一起。

normal.en: Re- means again, and pair means two things together: put the pair back together again.
normal.cn: re- 表示再次，pair 表示一对：把这一对重新拼回去。

normal.en: A repair shop is where broken pairs of parts are matched again.
normal.cn: repair shop 就是把断开的部件重新配上对的地方。

normal.en: The noun repair often follows under or for, as in under repair.
normal.cn: 名词 repair 常跟在 under 或 for 后面，如 under repair。

normal.en: Repair the damage is the phrase used when the damage is not physical.
normal.cn: repair the damage 用于非实物的损害。

normal.en: Compare reparable and irreparable: one can be paired again, one cannot.
normal.cn: 对比 reparable 与 irreparable：一个还能重新拼合，一个不能。

abstract.en: Picture a cracked cup held together while the glue sets.
abstract.cn: 想象一只裂开的杯子被按住，等胶水凝固。

abstract.en: Imagine a radio with its back open and one bright wire being replaced.
abstract.cn: 想象收音机打开后盖，一根亮色的线正在被换掉。

abstract.en: Think of two people who stopped talking and then carefully start again.
abstract.cn: 想象两个不再说话的人，又小心地重新开始交谈。

examples.en: The mechanic repaired the engine in two hours.
examples.cn: 机械师用两个小时修好了发动机。

examples.en: The school is raising money for roof repairs.
examples.cn: 学校正在筹钱维修屋顶。

examples.en: They met again to repair their friendship.
examples.cn: 他们再次见面，修复彼此的友谊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「瑞派尔」——瑞气把坏掉的东西派回原样；这只是谐音联想，与词源无关。

root: 拉丁语 re-（再次）+ parare（准备）→ reparare（重新准备好）→ 古法语 reparer → 中古英语 reparen，义为修补、使复原。

sensesIntro.en: One image of putting broken parts back together grows into three uses: fixing an object, the work of fixing, and restoring trust.
sensesIntro.cn: 「把破损零件拼回去」这一个画面长出三种用法：修好物件、维修工作本身，以及修复信任。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: broken parts brought back into line until the machine runs again.
core.cn: 核心意象：断开的零件被重新对齐，机器再次运转。

branches.en: Making a damaged object work again is the basic sense.
branches.cn: 让受损的物件重新可用，是最基本的义项。

branches.en: The action becomes a noun for the work and the state of being mended.
branches.cn: 这个动作转为名词，指维修工作以及被修好的状态。

branches.en: The same joining motion is applied to a broken relationship.
branches.cn: 同样的「接合」动作被用到破裂的关系上。

branches.en: Fixing and the fixing work are the verb and noun sides of one act.
branches.cn: 修理与维修工作是同一动作的动词面和名词面。

branches.en: Both object repair and relationship repair remove damage and restore use.
branches.cn: 物件修复与关系修复都在消除损害、恢复功能。

intro.en: Repair is built from a Latin prefix and a Latin verb stem, with a French verb ending carried into English.
intro.cn: repair 由拉丁前缀、拉丁动词词干和传入英语的法语动词词尾构成。

latinIntro.en: The prefix re- adds the idea of again, while parare means to prepare or make ready.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 re- 增添「再次」的意思，parare 表示「准备、使就绪」。

items.example: Re- returns in repair and restore.
items.exampleCN: re- 也出现在 repair 和 restore 中。

items.example: Parare is the stem behind repair.
items.exampleCN: parare 是 repair 背后的词干。
reparare 由 re- 与 parare 合成。

items.example: Old French reparer carries the word into English.
items.exampleCN: 古法语 reparer 把这个词带入英语。

items.example: Repair keeps the idea of making ready again.
items.exampleCN: repair 保留了「重新使就绪」的意思。

items.example: Reparable adds -able to the same stem.
The prefix ir- makes reparable negative.
items.exampleCN: 前缀 ir- 使 reparable 变成否定。

definition_zh: 回答；答复；回应
definition_en: to answer someone in words, in writing, or with an action
core_image: 一封信寄出去，几天后另一封信折返回来，落在同一个信箱里
scene: 她发出邮件后一直盯着屏幕，半小时后终于收到对方的回复。 She smiled when her colleague replied with a single word: yes.
sceneCN: 这里 reply 是「回复；答复」（第 2 个义项：以书面形式作答）；句意：同事只回了一个「是」，她笑了。

derivatives.zh: 答复者
回邮邮资已付的

senses.title: To answer in words
senses.definition: to say or write something as an answer to a question or message
senses.definitionCN: 针对问题或信息说出或写下回答
senses.example: He replied that he would arrive at noon.
senses.exampleCN: 他回答说中午到。
senses.why: The Latin verb replicare means to fold back, so a reply is words sent back to the one who spoke first.
senses.whyCN: 拉丁动词 replicare 意为「折回」，所以 reply 就是把话折回给先开口的人。

senses.title: A written answer
senses.definition: a written answer to a letter, email, or formal request
senses.definitionCN: 对信件、电子邮件或正式请求的书面答复
senses.example: I sent the report on Monday and am still waiting for a reply.
senses.exampleCN: 我周一发了报告，现在还在等回复。
senses.why: Writing is a channel for the same returning message, so the noun covers letters and emails.
senses.whyCN: 书写只是同一条「回传信息」的渠道，所以名词义项涵盖信件和邮件。

senses.title: To respond with an action
senses.definition: to react to an action with another action
senses.definitionCN: 用另一个行动来回应某个行动
senses.example: The soldiers replied to the attack with warning shots.
senses.exampleCN: 士兵鸣枪示警，作为对袭击的回应。
senses.why: When words give way to deeds, the fold-back pattern still holds, which extends reply to actions.
senses.whyCN: 当言语让位于行动时，「折回」的模式仍在，于是 reply 也扩展到行动。

intro.en: Reply comes through Old French from Latin replicare, to fold back, built from re- and plicare, to fold.
intro.cn: reply 经由古法语来自拉丁语 replicare（折回），由 re- 与 plicare（折叠）构成。

items.en: Plicare means to fold, bend, or weave.
items.cn: plicare 意为折叠、弯曲或编织。

items.en: Replicare adds re-, back, and means to fold something back on itself.
items.cn: replicare 加上 re-（回），意为把某物折回自身。

items.en: Replicare develops the sense of answering or responding to a charge.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语中，replicare 发展出「答复、回应指控」的意思。

items.en: Old French replier means to fold back and also to answer.
items.cn: 古法语 replier 既指折回，也指回答。

items.en: Middle English replien keeps the answer sense and drops the folding image.
items.cn: 中古英语 replien 保留「回答」义，折纸的画面逐渐淡去。

items.en: Modern English reply covers spoken, written, and acted responses.
items.cn: 现代英语 reply 涵盖口头、书面和行动上的回应。

note.en: Reply shares its Latin folding root with replica and replicate, while its meaning sits with answer and respond.
note.cn: reply 与 replica、replicate 共享拉丁语「折叠」词根，而词义上与 answer、respond 相邻。

entries.definition: an exact copy of an object
to copy something exactly
the act of copying or reproducing
to say something back to a question
to react to something said or done
to answer quickly, often sharply
to act in response to an event

normalIntro.en: Reply contains pli, the folding root also seen in ply and replicate, so the memory image is a message folded back to the sender.
normalIntro.cn: reply 含有 pli 这个「折叠」词根，也见于 ply 和 replicate，所以记忆画面是「把信息折回给发送者」。

normal.en: Re- means back, and ply means fold: fold the message back to the sender.
normal.cn: re- 表示回，ply 表示折：把信息折回给发送者。

normal.en: Reply to is the phrase that marks the person or message being answered.
normal.cn: reply to 标出被回复的人或信息。

normal.en: In reply is a fixed phrase meaning as an answer.
normal.cn: in reply 是固定短语，意为「作为答复」。

normal.en: No reply is what an empty inbox says.
normal.cn: no reply 就是空邮箱传达的状态。

normal.en: Compare replica: a replica is a copy folded back from an original.
normal.cn: 对比 replica：复制品是从原件「折回」的副本。

abstract.en: Picture a paper plane flying back to the hand that threw it.
abstract.cn: 想象纸飞机飞回扔出它的那只手。

abstract.en: Imagine a letter returning to the same mailbox days later.
abstract.cn: 想象几天后一封信回到同一个信箱。

abstract.en: Think of a question bouncing off a wall and coming back as an answer.
abstract.cn: 想象问题撞到墙上，反弹回来变成答案。

examples.en: She replied to the invitation the same day.
examples.cn: 她当天就回复了邀请。

examples.en: His reply was short but polite.
examples.cn: 他的回复简短而有礼貌。

examples.en: The company replied to the complaint with an apology.
examples.cn: 公司以道歉回应了投诉。

dict_mnemonic.text: re-（回）+ ply（折）＝把话折回去，即回答；这是拆词联想，不是谐音。

root: 拉丁语 re-（回）+ plicare（折叠）→ replicare（折回、答复）→ 古法语 replier → 中古英语 reply，指把话折回给发问者。

sensesIntro.en: A message folded back is the core: first spoken words, then written answers, then actions that answer actions.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是「把信息折回去」：先说出口的回答，再是书面答复，最后是以行动回应行动。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a message folded back to the person who sent the first one.
core.cn: 核心意象：信息被折回给最先发出它的那个人。

branches.en: Spoken words sent back are the original verbal sense.
branches.cn: 把话送回去，是最早的言语义项。

branches.en: A letter or email carries the same return into writing.
branches.cn: 信件或邮件把同样的「返回」带入书面形式。

branches.en: An action can answer another action, extending the pattern beyond words.
branches.cn: 一个行动可以回应另一个行动，使这个模式超出言语。

branches.en: Speech and writing are two channels of the same answer.
branches.cn: 口头与书面是同一个答复的两条渠道。

branches.en: Words and deeds both complete the return loop.
branches.cn: 言语与行动都完成同一条回环。

intro.cn: reply 是法语形态的动词，建立在拉丁前缀与拉丁「折叠」词根之上。

latinIntro.en: The prefix re- means back, and plicare means to fold, so replicare is to fold back.
latinIntro.cn: 前缀 re- 表示回，plicare 表示折叠，所以 replicare 就是「折回」。

items.exampleCN: re- 出现在 reply 与 return 开头。

items.example: Plicare is the folding root behind reply.
items.exampleCN: plicare 是 reply 背后的「折叠」词根。
replicare 由 re- 与 plicare 合成。
