items.exampleCN: replica 与 reply 共享「折叠」词根。

items.example: Replicate comes from the same Latin verb.
items.exampleCN: replicate 来自同一个拉丁动词。

definition_zh: 不；没有；并非；不太
definition_en: used to negate a verb, adjective or whole clause; also used to deny a noun phrase or to soften what is said
core_image: 一扇紧闭的门上挂着一块木牌，牌上只写着一个表示拒绝的字
scene: 门上挂着一块手写的木牌，路过的人凑近看了又看，随后转身离开。 The sign on the door said the shop would not open until noon.
sceneCN: 这里是「不」（第 1 个义项：否定动词、形容词或整个句子），句意为门上的告示说这家店要到中午才开门。图中可辨识物件：木牌、门把手、台阶。

derivatives.zh: 由 can 与 not 合成，义为「不能」，写作一个词
与 not 同出古英语的否定词，义为「零；无」
由 not 与 withstand 加 -ing 构成，义为「尽管；虽然」

senses.title: Used to negate a verb, adjective or clause
senses.titleCN: 不；没有（否定动词、形容词或句子）
senses.definition: used before a verb, adjective or adverb to say that something is not true, does not happen or is not the case
senses.definitionCN: 用在动词、形容词或副词前，表示某事不真实、不发生或不成立
senses.example: The sign on the door said the shop would not open until noon.
senses.exampleCN: 门上的告示说这家店要到中午才开门。
senses.why: The word began as a pronoun meaning no thing, and in unstressed positions it shrank into a bare negator that could sit in front of any verb and turn it negative.
senses.whyCN: 这个词最初是一个代词，意思是「没有东西」；在非重读的位置上它缩成一个光秃秃的否定词，可以放在任何动词前把动词变成否定。

senses.title: Used to deny a noun phrase or a statement
senses.titleCN: 不是；并非（否定名词或整句话）
senses.definition: used before a noun phrase, or in a short answer, to reject it rather than to describe an action
senses.definitionCN: 用在名词短语前，或用于简短回答，表示否定对方所说的内容，而不是描述某个动作
senses.example: Not everyone in the room agreed with the plan.
senses.exampleCN: 房间里并非每个人都同意这个计划。
senses.why: Once the pronoun lost its noun, the negator could stand before any phrase, not only before a verb, so it learned to reject a subject or an entire statement.
senses.whyCN: 代词丢掉后面的名词之后，这个否定词可以站在任何短语前面，而不只是动词前面，于是它学会了否定一个主语或整句话。

senses.title: Used to soften or limit what is said
senses.titleCN: 不太；并不（用于委婉或减弱语气）
senses.definition: used before a word to weaken a claim, as in not very, not quite or not necessarily
senses.definitionCN: 用在某个词前减弱语气，如 not very、not quite 或 not necessarily
senses.example: The result was not unexpected, but it was still a shock.
senses.exampleCN: 这个结果并不意外，但还是让人吃惊。
senses.why: A flat denial is blunt, so English puts the same negator in front of a weaker word to hold back the claim; the sentence stays negative while the tone turns careful.
senses.whyCN: 直截了当的否定太冲，于是英语把同一个否定词放在更弱的词前面，用来收住话头；句子仍是否定，语气却变得谨慎。

intro.en: Not began as a pronoun for no thing and was shortened into the general English negator; its oldest surviving relative is the word for nought.
intro.cn: not 最初是一个表示「没有东西」的代词，后来缩短成英语里通用的否定词；它现存最老的亲族是表示「零」的那个词。

items.en: Nā meant never or not and wiht meant a thing, so nāwiht said no thing and could stand alone as a pronoun.
items.cn: nā 表示「从不、不」，wiht 表示「东西」，因此 nāwiht 说的是「没有东西」，可以单独作代词使用。

items.en: In quick speech the pronoun was contracted to nāht, which served as the word for nothing and later for zero.
items.cn: 在快速的口语里，这个代词缩成 nāht，既用来表示「没有什么」，后来也用来表示「零」。

items.en: The unstressed form not split off from nought and took over as the ordinary negator, replacing the older pattern of ne before the verb.
items.cn: 非重读形式 not 从 nought 里分出来，取代了旧的「ne 加动词」格式，成为日常的否定词。

items.en: Do-support spread, and not attached itself to do, does and did, which is why modern questions and emphatic statements still use do not.
items.cn: 助动词 do 的用法扩展开来，not 便附着在 do、does、did 上，所以现代的问句和强调句仍用 do not。

items.en: Modern English also contracts not to n't, and keeps it in fixed frames such as not only and if not, where the negation shapes the whole sentence.
items.cn: 现代英语还把 not 缩写成 n't，并把它保留在 not only、if not 这类固定框架里，那里的否定塑造着整个句子。

note.en: The look-alike group collects words that share the old no-thing stem; the near-meaning group collects the other ways English denies or zeroes out a statement.
note.cn: 形近组收共享古老「无物」词干的词；近义组收英语中其他表示否定或归零的说法。

entries.definition: An older spelling of nought, meaning nothing or zero.
entries.definitionCN: nought 的较旧拼写，意为「无」或「零」。

entries.definition: The number zero, and in older use nothing at all.
entries.definitionCN: 数字零，旧时也指「什么都没有」。

entries.definition: A preposition meaning in spite of, built with not at its head.
entries.definitionCN: 以 not 开头的介词，义为「尽管」。

entries.definition: A determiner that denies the existence of a thing, as in no money.
entries.definitionCN: 限定词，否认某物的存在，如 no money。

entries.definition: At no time, the negator used for time rather than for a single action.
entries.definitionCN: 在任何时候都不，是用来否定时间的否定词。

entries.definition: Not one, or not any, a pronoun that stands in for a negated quantity.
entries.definitionCN: 一个也不、任何也不，是代替被否定数量的代词。

normalIntro.en: The word is a shrunken pronoun for no thing, and its whole history is a drift from a standalone word toward a small negator that hooks onto verbs.
normalIntro.cn: 这个词是一个缩小的「无物」代词，它的全部历史就是从独立词漂移成一个钩在动词前的小否定词。

normal.en: Old English nāwiht was nā plus wiht, no plus thing, so not and nothing come from the same source.
normal.cn: 古英语 nāwiht 是 nā 加 wiht，即「不」加「东西」，所以 not 与 nothing 同出一源。

normal.en: The unstressed form not broke away from nought and became the everyday way to deny a verb.
normal.cn: 非重读形式 not 从 nought 里脱离出来，成为日常否定动词的方式。

normal.en: Modern questions use do-support, so the negator rides on do, does or did rather than sitting alone.
normal.cn: 现代问句用助动词 do 支撑，所以否定词搭在 do、does 或 did 上，而不是单独站着。

normal.en: The contraction n't keeps the same word in a shorter shape, as in isn't and don't.
normal.cn: 缩写 n't 是同一个词的短形，如 isn't 与 don't。

normal.en: Fixed frames such as not only and if not show that not can negate a whole structure, not just one word.
normal.cn: not only 与 if not 这类固定框架说明，not 能否定整个结构，而不只是一个词。

abstract.en: A word that once meant no thing ended up as the smallest hinge in English grammar, turning any sentence the other way.
abstract.cn: 一个曾经表示「没有东西」的词，最后成了英语语法里最小的铰链，把任何句子转向反面。

abstract.en: Negation always costs a word, and English chose to shorten its oldest denial until only three letters were left.
abstract.cn: 否定总要花掉一个词，英语选择把最古老的否认一再缩短，直到只剩下三个字母。

abstract.en: Not is the quiet tool that lets a language say what is absent without naming it.
abstract.cn: not 是语言里一件安静的工具，让人不必说出缺席之物，也能说出它的缺席。

examples.en: The sign on the door said the shop would not open until noon.
examples.cn: 门上的告示说这家店要到中午才开门。

examples.en: Not everyone in the room agreed with the plan.
examples.cn: 房间里并非每个人都同意这个计划。

examples.en: The result was not unexpected, but it was still a shock.
examples.cn: 这个结果并不意外，但还是让人吃惊。

dict_mnemonic.text: 「诺特」——门上挂着牌子，只写一个否定的字；not 就是不。

root: 古英语 nāwiht（nā「不」加 wiht「东西」，即「无物」）缩为 nāht，中古英语非重读形式 not 独立出来，取代 ne 加动词的旧否定格式；同源词有 nought、nothing。

sensesIntro.en: The core is the denial of a thing; it then spreads to verbs and clauses, to short answers, and to softened or limited claims.
sensesIntro.cn: 核心是对「有某物」的否认；义项由此扩展到动词与句子、简短回答，以及被减弱或限制的说法。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a wooden sign hanging on a shut door, carrying a single mark of refusal.
core.cn: 核心意象：一扇紧闭的门上挂着一块木牌，牌上只有一个表示拒绝的记号。

branches.en: a door sign that turns a visitor away
branches.cn: 把来客挡回去的门上告示

branches.en: a switch flipped to the off position
branches.cn: 被扳到关闭位置的开关

branches.en: a raised hand rejecting a whole proposal
branches.cn: 举手否决整个提案

branches.en: a careful speaker holding back a strong word
branches.cn: 措辞谨慎的人收住一个重词

branches.en: one small word denying an act and denying a claim
branches.cn: 同一个短词既否定动作，也否定说法

intro.en: The word is built from an Old English negative particle and a noun for thing, then shortened and joined to English auxiliaries and contractions.
intro.cn: 这个词由古英语的否定小词与表示「东西」的名词构成，之后被缩短，并与英语助动词和缩写形式结合。

latinIntro.en: Not has no reliable Latin cognate; Latin negates with non and nihil, words of a different formation, so no Latin entry is listed.
latinIntro.cn: not 没有可靠的拉丁同族词；拉丁语用「non」与「nihil」表示否定，构词方式不同，因此不列拉丁词条。

definition_zh: 能量；能源；精力；活力；劲头
definition_en: the capacity to do work or cause change, the power supplied as electricity or fuel, or the vigour a person or group has
core_image: 一团向内收着的劲：看着不动，一旦放开就能推动别的东西。
scene: 马拉松最后一公里，选手们咬着牙留着力气。 She saved her energy for the last kilometre of the race.
sceneCN: 这里 energy 是「人的体力、精力」（第 3 个义项：个人活力）；句意：跑者们把体力留到最后一段爬坡。场景要点：半山腰、放慢的脚步、水壶。

derivatives.zh: 精力充沛的；有力的；高能的
精力充沛地；有力地
给……能量；激发；使通电
能量学；热力学分支
增能器；提神物；激励者

senses.title: Physics: capacity to do work
senses.definition: the capacity of a body or system to do work or produce change, measured in joules
senses.definitionCN: 物体或系统做功或产生变化的本领，以焦耳计
senses.example: The falling water converts potential energy into kinetic energy.
senses.exampleCN: 落下的水把势能转化为动能。
senses.why: Greek energeia was Aristotle's word for 'activity, actuality' — being at work. Physics took the word for whatever can be put to work.
senses.whyCN: 希腊语 energeia 是亚里士多德用来表示“活动、现实性”的词——正在起作用。物理学用它指“任何能被用来做功的东西”。

senses.title: Electricity supplied to users
senses.titleCN: 电力：送到用户家里的那部分
senses.definition: electricity as a supply that homes and industry consume
senses.definitionCN: 作为家庭与工业消耗的电力供应
senses.example: The town buys half its energy from a local wind farm.
senses.exampleCN: 这座镇上一半的电力购自当地风电场。
senses.why: The abstract capacity becomes a commodity once it is metered and billed. Energy here is a quantity delivered through a wire.
senses.whyCN: 一旦可以计量、可以计费，抽象的本领就变成了商品。这里的 energy 是通过电线送来的一个量。

senses.title: A person's vigour
senses.definition: the physical and mental strength that lets a person stay active
senses.definitionCN: 使人保持活动的体力与心力
senses.example: He had no energy left after the night shift.
senses.exampleCN: 夜班之后他一点力气都没有了。
senses.why: The body is treated as a system with a store of work-capacity. Spending it leaves less for the next task, exactly like a battery.
senses.whyCN: 身体被当成一个有做功存量的系统。用掉一些，下一件事就少一些，和电池一模一样。

senses.title: Force of expression
senses.titleCN: 语言的力量：表达的劲道
senses.definition: the force or vividness with which something is expressed
senses.definitionCN: 表达时所带的力度或生动性
senses.example: The speech lost its energy when the last paragraph was cut.
senses.exampleCN: 末段被删掉后，这篇演讲失去了劲道。
senses.why: This is the sense with which the word entered English in the 1590s: 'force of expression'. It came from a misreading of Aristotle's 'actuality'.
senses.whyCN: 这是这个词 16 世纪 90 年代进入英语时的意思：“表达的力量”。它来自对亚里士多德“现实性”的误读。

senses.title: The drive to act
senses.titleCN: 行动的劲头：愿意往前推
senses.definition: the motivation or drive that makes a person or group act
senses.definitionCN: 促使个人或群体行动的动机与冲劲
senses.example: The campaign ran on the energy of its volunteers.
senses.exampleCN: 这场运动靠志愿者的干劲运转。
senses.why: Work-capacity becomes willingness. A group with energy is one that can keep exerting itself, so the physical store turns into social drive.
senses.whyCN: 做功的存量变成了意愿。有 energy 的群体，是能持续使力的群体，物理存量由此变成社会动力。

senses.title: Fuel and resources for power
senses.titleCN: 能源资源：可烧、可转换的料
senses.definition: natural resources such as oil, gas, coal, or sunlight used to produce power
senses.definitionCN: 用于产能的石油、天然气、煤、阳光等自然资源
senses.example: The country is rich in energy but poor in water.
senses.exampleCN: 这个国家能源丰富，却缺水。
senses.why: The resource is potential work stored in matter. Calling oil 'energy' is shorthand for 'material that can release energy'.
senses.whyCN: 资源就是储存在物质里的潜在做功能力。把石油叫作 energy，是“能释放能量的物质”的简称。

senses.title: Energy in food
senses.titleCN: 食物热量：吃进去的燃料
senses.definition: the amount of heat or fuel value that a food provides to the body
senses.definitionCN: 食物为身体提供的热量或燃料价值
senses.example: Nuts are dense in energy for their size.
senses.exampleCN: 坚果个头小，热量却很密集。
senses.why: The body is an engine; food is its fuel. The same word covers both because both are measured in the same units.
senses.whyCN: 身体是发动机，食物是燃料。同一个词覆盖两者，因为它们用同样的单位计量。

senses.title: Vitality of a place or scene
senses.titleCN: 场所的活力：人多、事多、劲足
senses.definition: the liveliness and activity that a place, market, or social scene has
senses.definitionCN: 某个地方、市场或社交场面所具有的生气与活跃度
senses.example: The old port has a creative energy it lacked in the 1990s.
senses.exampleCN: 这座老港区有一种 1990 年代没有的创造活力。
senses.why: The metaphor widens again: a place is a system that can be more or less at work, and its visible activity is its energy.
senses.whyCN: 比喻再度扩大：一个地方是一个可多可少“在运转”的系统，它可见的活跃就是它的能量。

senses.title: Effort directed at a task
senses.titleCN: 投入的精力：把劲用在哪
senses.definition: the effort or attention that someone chooses to give to a particular activity
senses.definitionCN: 某人选择投入某项活动的努力或注意力
senses.example: She put most of her energy into teaching rather than research.
senses.exampleCN: 她把大部分精力放在教学而不是研究上。
senses.why: Energy is finite, so putting it somewhere implies taking it from somewhere else. The word becomes a way of talking about allocation.
senses.whyCN: 能量有限，投到某处就意味着从别处拿走。这个词由此成了谈论“分配”的方式。

intro.en: Energy comes from Aristotle's Greek word for 'being at work'. It entered English meaning 'force of expression', turned into 'power' in the 17th century, and only became a scientific term in 1807.
intro.cn: energy 来自亚里士多德表示“正在起作用”的希腊词。它进入英语时意为“表达的力量”，17 世纪转为“力量”，直到 1807 年才成为科学术语。

items.en: Ergon meant 'work, deed, action'. It goes back to PIE *werg- 'to do', the root behind English work and wright.
items.cn: ergon 意为“工作、行为、行动”。它上溯到原始印欧语 *werg-“做”，是英语 work 与 wright 的词根。

items.en: Energeia was 'activity, action, operation'. Aristotle used it for 'actuality, reality, existence', as opposed to potential.
items.cn: energeia 意为“活动、行动、运作”。亚里士多德用它表示“现实性、实在、存在”，与“潜能”相对。

items.en: Late Latin borrowed the Greek word but misread Aristotle's 'actuality' as 'force of expression' — the power that calls up realistic pictures in the mind.
items.cn: 晚期拉丁语借入了这个希腊词，却把亚里士多德的“现实性”误读为“表达的力量”——那种能在心里唤起逼真图景的力量。

items.en: French énergie carried the Latin sense into English. English records energy in the 1590s meaning 'force of expression'.
items.cn: 法语 énergie 把拉丁义带进英语。英语在 16 世纪 90 年代记录 energy，意为“表达的力量”。

items.en: The broader sense 'power' is first recorded in the 1660s. The scientific use, as a measurable quantity, dates from 1807.
items.cn: 较宽的“力量”义最早记录于 17 世纪 60 年代。作为可测量的量，科学用法始于 1807 年。

items.en: Energy crisis is attested from 1970. The word now covers electricity bills, gym sessions, and the mood of a city, all from one Greek verb for work.
items.cn: energy crisis 于 1970 年见于记录。这个词如今覆盖电费单、健身课与城市气氛，全都出自同一个表示“工作”的希腊动词。

note.en: The first group shares the Greek ergon 'work' root; the second collects words for power and vigour.
note.cn: 第一组共享希腊语 ergon“工作”词根；第二组收“力量与活力”类词。

entries.definition: full of energy; active and forceful. It adds -etic to the Greek stem, not a separate root.
entries.definitionCN: 精力充沛的；活跃有力的。它把 -etic 加在希腊词干上，不是另一个词根。

entries.definition: to give energy to something, or to supply electricity to a device
entries.definitionCN: 给某物能量；给设备通电（由 energy 派生）

entries.definition: extra effect produced by two things working together. Greek syn- 'together' + ergon 'work'.
entries.definitionCN: 两物协作产生的额外效果。希腊语 syn-“共同”+ ergon“工作”。

entries.definition: a small unit of energy in the centimetre-gram-second system, named directly from Greek ergon 'work'.
entries.definitionCN: 厘米-克-秒制中的小能量单位，直接由希腊语 ergon“工作”命名。

entries.definition: in physics, the rate at which energy is used; in daily life, electricity or influence. It is not the same quantity as energy.
entries.definitionCN: 物理上指能量被使用的速率；日常指电力或影响力。它与 energy 不是同一个量。

entries.definition: a push or pull that can change motion. Force acts on a body; energy is what the body has or transfers.
entries.definitionCN: 能改变运动的推或拉。力作用于物体；能量是物体拥有或转移的东西。

entries.definition: the quality of being alive and full of strength. It is close to energy in the personal sense but more about life itself.
entries.definitionCN: 有生命且充满力量的状态。它接近 energy 的个人义，但更关于“生命本身”。

entries.definition: strength and enthusiasm in action. It is more formal than energy and often about sustained effort.
entries.definitionCN: 行动中的力量与热情。它比 energy 正式，常指持续的用力。

entries.definition: the ability to keep going for a long time. It is energy measured over duration.
entries.definitionCN: 长时间坚持下去的能力。它可说是以“持续时间”计量的 energy。

normalIntro.en: Real parts and relatives: Greek en 'at' + ergon 'work', giving energeia 'activity'; family words energetic, energize, energetics, synergy, erg, and the native English work from the same PIE root.
normalIntro.cn: 只用真实成分与同族词：希腊语 en“在”+ ergon“工作”，合成 energeia“活动”；词族为 energetic、energize、energetics、synergy、erg，以及同源印欧词根的本土词 work。

normal.en: Ergon is 'work'; energy is the capacity for work, whichever form it is stored in.
normal.cn: ergon 是“工作”；energy 就是“做功的本领”，无论它以什么形式储存。

normal.en: Synergy is syn- 'together' + ergon: work that only happens when two things cooperate.
normal.cn: synergy 是 syn-“共同”+ ergon：只有两物协作才出现的工作效果。

normal.en: The word first meant 'force of expression' — a speech can have energy before a battery can.
normal.cn: 这个词最初指“表达的力量”——演讲能比电池更早有 energy。

normal.en: Power and energy are not the same: power is how fast energy is used.
normal.cn: power 与 energy 不同：power 是能量被使用的快慢。

normal.en: A food label in calories is an energy label, because the body is an engine.
normal.cn: 食品标签上的卡路里就是能量标签，因为身体是一台发动机。

abstract.en: Energy is the only currency every system accepts.
abstract.cn: 能量是唯一被所有系统接受的货币。

abstract.en: What you spend your energy on is the truest statement of what you value.
abstract.cn: 你把精力花在哪里，是对你在乎什么最真实的陈述。

abstract.en: Actuality is the old meaning: to have energy is to be, not merely to be able to be.
abstract.cn: actuality 是它古老的含义：有能量即是“在”，而不只是“可能在”。

examples.en: Solar panels turn sunlight into electrical energy.
examples.cn: 太阳能板把阳光转化为电能。

examples.en: She threw all her energy into getting the clinic reopened.
examples.cn: 她把全部精力投入到让诊所重新开张。

examples.en: The debate lost energy once the two main speakers left.
examples.cn: 两位主要发言人一走，辩论就失去了劲道。

dict_mnemonic.text: “摁呢挤”——把最后一点劲儿摁住、再挤出来，人还能往前推 → energy 能量、精力

root: 源自希腊语 energeia“活动、现实性”，由 en“在”+ ergon“工作”构成（ergon 上溯原始印欧语 *werg-“做”，与英语 work 同源）；经晚期拉丁语 energia、法语 énergie 进入英语，16 世纪 90 年代义为“表达的力量”，17 世纪 60 年代转为“力量”，1807 年成为科学术语。

sensesIntro.en: Nine senses of energy, all one quantity: a store of capacity for work, appearing as electricity, fuel, vigour, or expressive force.
sensesIntro.cn: energy 的九个义项是同一个量：做功能力的储存，以电力、燃料、体力或表达力等形式出现。

core.en: CORE IMAGE: a compressed spring or a charged cell, quiet but holding a push inside it.
core.cn: 核心意象：压紧的弹簧或充好电的电池，安静地收着一股推力。

branches.en: MEASURED: joules, barrels, and calories are three ways of counting the same capacity.
branches.cn: 可计量：焦耳、桶、卡路里，是同一个本领的三种数法。

branches.en: DELIVERED: electricity is energy turned into a billed commodity moving through a wire.
branches.cn: 已送达：电力是能量变成可计费的商品，沿电线流动。

branches.en: PERSONAL: a body, a will, and a schedule all run on a finite store that must be allocated.
branches.cn: 个人：身体、意志与日程都靠一个有限存量运转，必须分配。

branches.en: EXPRESSION: the oldest English sense, where a sentence carries force the way a battery carries charge.
branches.cn: 表达：英语中最古老的义项，一句话带着力量，就像电池带着电荷。

branches.en: PLACES: a city or market can be more or less at work, and we read its activity as energy.
branches.cn: 场所：城市或市场可多可少地“在运转”，我们把它可见的活跃读作 energy。

intro.en: Energy's family is Greek ergon 'work' dressed in English endings. Suffixes mark the adjective, the adverb, the verb, and the science; compounds name the industries built on the quantity.
intro.cn: energy 的词族是希腊语 ergon“工作”穿上英语词尾。后缀标记形容词、副词、动词与学科；复合词则命名建立在这个量上的产业。

latinIntro.en: The reliable forms are Greek energeia, energos, and ergon, borrowed into Late Latin as energia. Latin added no new root; it passed the Greek word on.
latinIntro.cn: 可靠的形式是希腊语 energeia、energos、ergon，以 energia 的形式借入晚期拉丁语。拉丁语没有新增词根，只是把这个希腊词传了下去。

items.meaningCN: 精力充沛的；活跃的（-ic 构成形容词，17 世纪 50 年代始见）
items.exampleCN: 她是一位精力充沛的活动家。

items.meaningCN: 有力地；精力充沛地（-ally 构成副词）
items.example: He argued energetically against the plan.
items.exampleCN: 他激烈地反对这个计划。

items.meaning: to give energy to; to power a device
items.meaningCN: 给……能量；给设备通电（-ize 构成动词）
items.example: The speech energized the whole team.
items.exampleCN: 这场演讲让整个团队振作起来。

items.meaning: the study of energy and its transformations
items.meaningCN: 研究能量及其转化的学科（-ics 构成学科名词）
items.example: The course begins with thermodynamics and energetics.
items.exampleCN: 这门课从热力学与能量学讲起。

items.meaning: something that gives energy, such as a tonic or a charger
items.meaningCN: 提供能量之物，如提神饮料或充电装置（-er 构成施事名词）
items.example: The charger is a fast energizer for the drone.
items.exampleCN: 这个充电器能快速给无人机补能。

items.meaning: combined effect greater than the sum of separate effects
items.meaningCN: 大于各部分单独效果之和的联合效应（同一 ergon 词根）
items.example: The merger promised synergy but delivered layoffs.
items.exampleCN: 合并承诺协同增效，结果却带来裁员。

items.meaningCN: 一个小能量单位（直接取自 ergon）
items.example: One joule equals ten million ergs.
items.exampleCN: 一焦耳等于一千万尔格。

items.meaning: using less energy for the same result
items.meaningCN: 以更少能量取得同样效果的
items.example: The new pumps are far more energy-efficient.

items.meaning: requiring a large amount of energy to produce
items.meaningCN: 生产时需要大量能源的

items.meaning: a severe shortage of fuel or power
items.meaningCN: 燃料或电力的严重短缺（1970 年始见）
items.example: The 1973 oil shock triggered a global energy crisis.
items.exampleCN: 1973 年石油冲击引发了全球能源危机。

definition_zh: 十字；交叉；穿越；穿过；杂交
definition_en: a mark or shape of two crossing lines; to go from one side to the other
core_image: 两条线在路口相互穿过
scene: 放学路上，我们在人行横道前停下来，等绿灯亮起才走。 Remember to look both ways before you cross the road.
sceneCN: 这里 cross 是「穿过；穿越」（第 2 个义项：从一边走到另一边）；句意是过马路前记得先两边看看。

derivatives.zh: 由动词加 -ing 构成，义为「交叉点；渡口；人行横道」
复合词，义为「人行横道」
复合词，义为「十字路口」
由 cross 加 -wise 构成，义为「交叉地」

senses.title: The shape or mark of two crossing lines
senses.definition: a mark or object shaped like the letter x or a plus sign, often a symbol
senses.definitionCN: 像字母 x 或加号形状的记号或物体，常用作符号
senses.example: She drew a small cross on the map to show our meeting place.
senses.exampleCN: 她在地图上画了个小十字，标出集合地点。
senses.why: The core image is two lines striking through each other, so the shape itself is a cross.
senses.whyCN: 核心意象是两条线相互穿过，所以这个形状本身就是 cross。

senses.title: To go from one side to the other
senses.definition: to move from one side of a place, road or river to the other
senses.definitionCN: 从马路、河流等的一侧移动到另一侧
senses.example: Hold my hand while we cross the street.
senses.exampleCN: 过马路时牵着我的手。
senses.why: When you walk where two lines meet, you pass from one side to the other, so crossing lines became crossing places.
senses.whyCN: 走在两条线相交处时，你会从一侧到另一侧，所以交叉线引申出穿越义。

senses.title: To mix one line or kind with another
senses.definition: to put two kinds together, such as animals, plants or ideas
senses.definitionCN: 把两种东西放在一起，如动植物或想法
senses.example: Farmers cross two kinds of wheat to get better grain.
senses.exampleCN: 农民把两种小麦杂交以获得更好的谷物。
senses.why: Two lines meet and merge into one path, so two kinds joined become a cross.
senses.whyCN: 两条线相遇并汇成一条路，所以混合的两种事物也叫 cross。

senses.title: Angry or annoyed
senses.definition: slightly angry or annoyed, mainly in British English
senses.definitionCN: 有点生气或恼火，主要用于英式英语
senses.example: Mom was cross when she saw the messy room.
senses.exampleCN: 看到凌乱的房间，妈妈生气了。
senses.why: Some say a frown draws crossing lines on the forehead, which may link the mood to the shape; the link is a guess.
senses.whyCN: 有人说皱眉会在额头画交叉线，也许因此把情绪和形状联系起来；这只是一种猜测。

intro.en: Cross travelled from Latin through Old Norse into English.
intro.cn: cross 从拉丁语经古诺斯语传入英语。

items.en: The Latin crux meant a cross, a frame or stake, later a hard point of a problem.
items.cn: 拉丁语 crux 意为十字架、刑架，后指问题的难点。

items.en: Old Norse brought kross to England with the early church.
items.cn: 古诺斯语把 kross 随早期基督教带到英格兰。

items.en: Old English used cros for the Christian symbol.
items.cn: 古英语用 cros 指基督教的十字符号。

items.en: The verb sense of going across and the mixed-line sense grew from the shape.
items.cn: 穿越与混合的动词义由这个形状发展而来。

items.en: Modern speech adds the angry sense and many compounds like crosswalk.
items.cn: 现代口语增加了生气的义项和 crosswalk 等复合词。

note.en: These words share the cross family or meet its shape idea.
note.cn: 这些词属于 cross 词族，或与交叉形状相关。

abstract.cn: 画一个加号，然后把它当作街角走一遍。

abstract.en: Picture two family lines of wheat merging into one field.
abstract.cn: 想象两条小麦家族线汇成同一片田。

examples.en: We waited at the crosswalk, then crossed safely.
examples.cn: 我们在人行横道等灯，然后安全穿过马路。

examples.en: Cross out the wrong answer and write again.

examples.en: Don't be cross; we can fix the model together.

definition_zh: 东方的；东部的；朝东的
definition_en: lying in or coming from the east, or related to the eastern part of a place
core_image: 地图上被朝阳镀亮的那一侧
scene: 清晨的地图课上，老师把挂图转向窗边的光线。 The eastern coast of the island catches the first sunlight.
sceneCN: 这里 eastern 是「东部的」（第 1 个义项：位于或来自东方的）；句意：海岛的东部海岸迎接着第一缕阳光。

collocations.phrase: the eastern part of the city

derivatives.zh: eastern 的基础方位词，义为「东；东方」
east 加 ward 构成，义为「向东」

senses.title: Lying in or toward the east
senses.definition: in or toward the east, or of the eastern part of an area
senses.definitionCN: 位于或朝向东方，或属于某区域的东部
senses.example: The eastern coast of the island catches the first sunlight.
senses.exampleCN: 海岛的东部海岸迎来第一缕阳光。
senses.why: The direction of sunrise is pinned onto a piece of land.
senses.whyCN: 日出的方位被钉在了一片土地上。

senses.title: Coming from the east
senses.definition: moving or blowing from the east
senses.definitionCN: 从东方来、朝其他方向移动或吹送
senses.example: An eastern wind brought the smell of rain.
senses.exampleCN: 东风带来了雨的气味。
senses.why: The region lends its name to whatever flows out of it.
senses.whyCN: 这片地域把名字借给了从中流出之物。

senses.title: Of eastern cultures
senses.definition: belonging to the countries and cultures of the east
senses.definitionCN: 属于东方国家与文化的
senses.example: He studies eastern philosophy at the university.
senses.exampleCN: 他在大学研究东方哲学。
senses.why: The compass direction becomes a cultural world.
senses.whyCN: 罗盘上的方位变成了一个文化世界。

intro.en: Eastern is east plus the old -ern ending that turns directions into adjectives.
intro.cn: eastern 就是 east 加上古老的 -ern 后缀，把方位变成形容词。

items.en: The root *austam meant the direction of dawn.
items.cn: 词根 *austam 意为黎明的方向。

items.en: Old English ēast named the sunrise direction.
items.cn: 古英语 ēast 指日出之方。

items.en: The ending -erne, seen in northern and southern, made direction adjectives.
items.cn: 后缀 -erne（见于 northern、southern）用来构成方位形容词。

items.en: Middle English esterne covered lands, winds and peoples of the east.
items.cn: 中古英语 esterne 涵盖东方的土地、风与民族。

items.en: Modern English fixed eastern for geography and for cultures.
items.cn: 现代英语把 eastern 用于地理与文化两域。

note.en: These words stand near eastern in form or in meaning.
note.cn: 这些词在形式或意义上与 eastern 相邻。

definition_zh: 使失望；使落空；辜负（期望）
definition_en: to make someone sad because something hoped for did not happen
core_image: 孩子眼里的气球慢慢瘪了下去
scene: 运动会上，接力赛只拿了第四名。 The result disappointed us, but our teacher cheered us up.
sceneCN: 这里 disappoint 是「使失望」（第 1 个义项：让盼望落空）；句意是这个结果让我们失望，但老师鼓励了我们。

derivatives.zh: 过去分词作形容词，义为「感到失望的」
现在分词作形容词，义为「令人失望的」
disappoint 加名词后缀构成，义为「失望；令人失望的事」
同根词，义为「任命」

senses.title: To let hopes fall
senses.definition: to make someone sad because a hope or plan fails
senses.definitionCN: 因希望或计划落空而让人难过
senses.example: The rain disappointed our plan for a picnic.
senses.exampleCN: 下雨让我们的野餐计划泡汤了。
senses.why: To appoint was to arrange or fix a thing in place; dis- undoes the arrangement, and the hope falls flat.
senses.whyCN: appoint 本义是「安排妥当」，dis- 解除了这种安排，希望随之落空。

senses.title: To fail to meet expectations
senses.definition: to be worse than someone expected
senses.definitionCN: 比预期差
senses.example: The film promised much but disappointed its fans.
senses.exampleCN: 这部电影预告很吸引人，却让影迷失望。
senses.why: When a fixed arrangement breaks, expectations break with it.
senses.whyCN: 安排一旦落空，期望也随之破碎。

intro.en: Disappoint is appoint plus dis-, and appoint meant to arrange.
intro.cn: disappoint 是 appoint 加 dis-，appoint 本义为「安排」。

items.en: Old French apointer meant to arrange or settle a matter.
items.cn: 古法语 apointer 意为安排、处理事务。

items.en: The root point here meant a fixed state, from Latin punctum (a point).
items.cn: 这里的词根 point 指固定状态，出自拉丁语 punctum（点）。

items.en: Middle French desappointer meant to undo an arrangement, to break a promise.
items.cn: 中古法语 desappointer 意为解除安排、失信。

items.en: English borrowed disappoint in the fifteenth century.
items.cn: 十五世纪英语借入 disappoint。

items.en: Later the word centred on broken hopes rather than broken appointments.
items.cn: 后来词义集中于落空的希望，而非被取消的约定。

note.en: These words share the appoint root or the sad-expectation field.
note.cn: 这些词同出 appoint 词根，或属于期望落空义场。

senses.title: In an easy way
senses.definition: in a way that is easy to understand or do
senses.definitionCN: 以容易理解或做到的方式
senses.example: The machine is simply designed.
senses.exampleCN: 这台机器的设计很简单。
senses.why: This is the adverb form of simple.
senses.whyCN: 这是 simple 的副词形式。

senses.title: Only or just
senses.definition: used to stress that something is no more than what is said
senses.definitionCN: 用于强调不过如此
senses.example: He simply wanted to help.
senses.exampleCN: 他只是想帮忙。
senses.why: The idea of no extra part grows into just.
senses.whyCN: 「没有多余部分」的念头引申为「只是」。

senses.title: Plainly
senses.definition: used to stress a plain fact
senses.definitionCN: 用于强调显而易见的事实
senses.example: The view was simply beautiful.
senses.exampleCN: 那景色简直美极了。
senses.why: A plain statement needs no ornament.
senses.whyCN: 平实的陈述不需要装饰。
